When collecting a gas over water, it is important to
correct_answer: correct for the vapor pressure of water
wrong_answers: {"set the temperature at 0°C","be sure the gas does not burn","wait until the barometer reads 760"}
explanation: Water vapor pressure affects the partial pressures of gases, so correction is essential for accurate gas volume measurements and calculations.

title: The principal source of Earth’s internal energy is
explanation: Earth's internal heat is primarily generated by radioactive decay of uranium, thorium, and potassium in the core and mantle.

title: A barometer that uses water instead of mercury will be
explanation: Since water is less dense than mercury, a water barometer must be taller (approximately 13.6 times) to exert equal atmospheric pressure.

title: The birth of an urban industrial workforce in Europe contributed to the start of the
wrong_answers: {"First Agricultural Revolution.","Third Agricultural Revolution.","Fourth Agricultural Revolution."}
explanation: The Second Agricultural Revolution was driven by industrialization and urban demand, spurring improvements in farming technology and practices in 18th-century Europe.

title: Which subfield of anthropology has been described as studying "other people's garbage"?
explanation: Archaeology studies past human societies through material remains and artifacts, sometimes humorously described as analyzing discarded waste.

title: Which of the following is a remote-sensing device used at archaeological sites?
explanation: Ground-penetrating radar, proton magnetometry, and electrical resistivity imaging are all non-invasive remote sensing techniques used in archaeological surveys.

title: What is the second number in the row of Pascal's triangle that has 43 numbers?
explanation: The 43rd row of Pascal's triangle has 43 numbers; the second number is always n−1 = 43−1 = 42.

title: Which of these animals is a rodent?
explanation: Beavers are large herbivorous rodents (family Castoridae); bats are chiropterans, wolverines are carnivores, and koalas are marsupials.

title: What was the required labor service owed to the king in return for the privilege of using property owned by the Incan empire?
explanation: Mit'a was the Inca labor obligation system requiring tribute work on state projects; khipu were recording devices, not labor services.

title: Krishna and Rama are incarnations of which Hindu god?
explanation: Vishnu is the preserver deity in Hinduism; Krishna and Rama are his most celebrated avatars (incarnations) in Hindu mythology.

title: As of 2016, about what percentage of adults aged 18 years or older were overweight?
explanation: According to 2016 WHO data, approximately 40% of adults globally were overweight (BMI ≥25), including those classified as obese.

title: Which god supplanted the earlier Mesopotamian supreme god Enil?
explanation: Marduk rose to supremacy among Mesopotamian gods during Babylon's political ascendance, replacing the earlier sky god Enlil in importance.

title: Which of the following is the correct characteristic of arteries?
correct_answer: They carry blood away from the heart.
wrong_answers: {"They are thin-walled blood vessels.","They contain valves that prevent backflow.","They always carry oxygenated blood."}
explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart; they have thick muscular walls, though not all arterial blood is oxygenated (pulmonary arteries).

title: The concentration of production activities and people spatially to benefit everyone is called
explanation: Agglomeration describes spatial concentration of industries and people that creates economies of scale and network benefits for all participants.

title: What does the phrase Guru-Panth mean within the Sikh traditions?
explanation: Guru-Panth in Sikhism means 'the way of the Guru,' representing the collective community as the spiritual authority after the ten historical Gurus.

title: The mudras, which are an important feature of Buddhist art, are also known as what?
explanation: Mudras are symbolic hand and finger gestures used in Buddhist, Hindu, and Taoist art and meditation to convey spiritual meanings and states.

title: The four big moons of Jupiter are Callisto Europa Ganymede and Io. Which one of them has the smallest distance to Jupiter?
explanation: Io is Jupiter's innermost of the four Galilean moons, orbiting at approximately 421,700 km from the planet's center.

title: What term describes the passing of genetic traits from one generation to the next?
explanation: Heredity is the biological transmission of traits from parents to offspring through genetic material (DNA) passed across generations.

title: Which of these is not a fabric?
explanation: Celotex is a brand of cellulose fiberboard insulation material; Velveteen, Seersucker, and Tencel are all woven or knitted fabrics.

title: Which of these household pets should be vaccinated for parvovirus?
explanation: Dogs are commonly vaccinated against canine parvovirus; hamsters, cats, and birds do not require this specific vaccine.

title: What proportion of vegans is likely to be deficient in vitamin B12?
explanation: Studies estimate approximately 32% of vegans have vitamin B12 deficiency due to limited dietary sources of this nutrient.

title: Which bodhisattva is known for conducting the souls of dead children to salvation?
explanation: Ojizo-sama is the bodhisattva associated with protecting children and guiding deceased children's souls to salvation in Japanese Buddhism.

title: I am a number. I have 7 in the ones place. I am less than 80 but greater than 70. What is my number?
explanation: The number with 7 in the ones place between 70 and 80 is 77.

title: In what year did the United States last win an Olympic gold medal in men's ice hockey?
explanation: The US men's ice hockey team won Olympic gold in 1980 at Lake Placid with their famous 'Miracle on Ice' victory over the Soviet Union.

title: What is the molar mass of a monoprotic weak acid that requires 26.3 mL of 0.122 M KOH to neutralize 0.682 gram of the acid?
explanation: Using moles of base (26.3 mL × 0.122 M), moles of acid equals moles of base; molar mass = 0.682 g ÷ (0.026 mol) ≈ 212 g/mol.

title: Which types of functions grow the slowest?
explanation: O(log log N) grows slowest; O(log e^N) = O(N), which is faster than O(log log N).

title: Find the number that makes the statement 12 over 18 = ? over 9 true.
explanation: Setting up the proportion: 12/18 = ?/9 gives ? = (12 × 9)/18 = 4.

title: In the author's two-hour movie representing the history of the universe, when do the earliest members of the human family appear?
correct_answer: during the final 3 seconds of the film
wrong_answers: {"at the beginning of the film","about half way through the film","90 minutes into the film"}
explanation: Carl Sagan's famous '13.8 billion year' cosmic calendar compressed to two hours shows humans appearing only in the final 3 seconds.

title: What does it mean to work 'probono'?
wrong_answers: {"work overtime","work as your own boss","not work at all"}
explanation: 'Pro bono publico' (for the public good) means professional work performed without charge, typically used in legal and medical fields.

title: As of 2019, about what percentage of the global population does not have access to safe drinking water?
explanation: As of 2019, approximately 30% of the global population lacked access to safe drinking water, primarily in Africa and South Asia.

explanation: The isupper() method in Python 3 returns True if all cased characters in a string are uppercase.

title: Which of these candy bars was named for a baseball player?
explanation: The Reggie Bar was named after baseball star Reggie Jackson; it launched in 1978 and was marketed during his Yankees career.
