explanation: Plutonium-244 is the most stable isotope with a half-life of 80 million years; it has 94 protons and 150 neutrons in its nucleus.

title: What part of the brain takes its name from the Greek for seahorse?
explanation: The hippocampus gets its name from the Greek 'hippokampos' (seahorse) due to its curved shape; it plays a crucial role in memory formation.

title: What does CPR, the emergency procedure to assist someone who has suffered cardiac arrest, stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Chronic pain relief","Cancer pain release","Contraceptive prevalence rate"}
explanation: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation combines chest compressions and rescue breathing to restore circulation and breathing in cardiac arrest victims.

title: The medial meniscus forms which part of what joint in the human body?
explanation: The medial meniscus is a cartilage pad in the knee joint that absorbs shock and distributes load between the femur and tibia.

title: The "Tibia" is found in which part of the body?
explanation: The tibia (shinbone) is the larger of the two leg bones below the knee; it bears most of the body's weight while the fibula provides stability.

title: Which of the following is considered classical conditioning?
wrong_answers: {"Skinner box experiment","Schrödinger's cat experiment","Harlow’s monkey experiments"}
explanation: Pavlov's dogs learned to salivate at the sound of a bell (conditioned stimulus) paired with food (unconditioned stimulus), defining classical conditioning principles.

title: Which horizon in a soil profile consists of bedrock?
explanation: The R horizon represents bedrock (parent material) in the soil profile; O contains organic matter, B is subsoil, and D is the weathered parent material.

title: Muscle fiber is constructed of bundles small long organelles called what?
explanation: Myofibrils are long, tubular structures containing contractile proteins (actin and myosin) that generate muscle force through sliding filament interactions.

title: How many types of quarks are there in the standard model of physics?
explanation: The standard model describes six quarks: up, down, charm, strange, top, and bottom; they combine to form protons, neutrons, and other hadrons.

title: 71% of the Earth's surface is made up of
explanation: Oceans and seas cover approximately 71% of Earth's surface, containing 97% of the planet's water and generating most oxygen through photosynthetic algae.

title: When the Falcon Heavy was launched on it's test flight, what was the only part of the operation that failed?
wrong_answers: {"Side Booster Landing","Deployment of Starman","Ignition and Liftoff"}
explanation: The Falcon Heavy test flight in February 2018 successfully deployed Starman and landed both side boosters, but the center core missed the barge landing.

title: Which planet did the "Viking 1" spacecraft send surface images of, starting in 1976?
explanation: Viking 1 landed on Mars on July 20, 1976, becoming the first spacecraft to successfully land and operate on the Martian surface.

title: What causes the sound of a heartbeat?
wrong_answers: {"Contraction of the heart chambers","Blood exiting the heart","Relaxation of the heart chambers"}
explanation: The 'lubb-dupp' heartbeat sound is caused by valve closure: the first sound marks atrioventricular valve closure, the second marks semilunar valve closure.

title: Which is not a type of neuron?
explanation: Perceptual neuron is not a recognized neuron type; the three main types are sensory (afferent), motor (efferent), and interneurons.

title: Botanically speaking, which of these fruits is NOT a berry?
explanation: Botanically, a true berry develops from a single ovary and includes bananas and grapes; strawberries are aggregate fruits made from multiple ovaries.

title: A comet's gaseous envelope (which creates the tail) is called what?
explanation: The coma is the gaseous envelope surrounding a comet's nucleus, created by solar radiation vaporizing ices and producing the visible tail.

title: The medical term for the belly button is which of the following?
explanation: The umbilicus (belly button) is the scar tissue remaining after umbilical cord severance at birth; its anatomy varies among individuals.

title: What is the official name of the star located closest to the North Celestial Pole?
explanation: Polaris (the North Star) is located within one degree of the North Celestial Pole, making it the primary navigation star for northern hemisphere observers.

title: What is the atomic number of the element Strontium?
explanation: Strontium (Sr) has atomic number 38, placing it among the alkaline earth metals with properties similar to calcium.

title: What is the scientific name for the extinct hominin known as "Lucy"?
explanation: Lucy (AL 288-1) belongs to Australopithecus afarensis, a hominin species that lived 3.2 million years ago and showed bipedal characteristics.

title: This element, when overcome with extreme heat and pressure, creates diamonds.
explanation: Carbon under extreme pressure (typically 3-4 million times atmospheric pressure) at high temperature (1,000-2,500°C) undergoes crystallographic transformation to diamond.

title: What is the standard SI unit for distance?
explanation: The metre is the fundamental SI unit for length, defined since 1983 as the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

title: What part of the body produces insulin?
explanation: The pancreas contains beta cells in the Islets of Langerhans that synthesize and secrete insulin in response to elevated blood glucose.

title: What nucleotide pairs with guanine?
explanation: Cytosine pairs with guanine in DNA through three hydrogen bonds; adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds.

title: Which of these is a type of stretch/deep tendon reflex?
explanation: The ankle jerk reflex is a monosynaptic stretch reflex where tapping the Achilles tendon causes automatic plantarflexion; gag and pupillary reflexes are cranial.

title: What causes Lyme disease?
explanation: Lyme disease is caused by the spirochete bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi, transmitted by infected Ixodes tick bites, typically in spring and summer.

title: What is radiation measured in?
explanation: The Gray (Gy) is the SI unit for absorbed radiation dose, defined as one joule of ionizing radiation energy per kilogram of matter.

title: Which of the following blood vessels carries deoxygenated blood?
explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; other vessels listed carry oxygenated blood.

title: Which of these choices is not one of the phases of mitosis?
explanation: Diplophase is not a recognized mitosis phase; the four phases are prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.

title: All the following metal elements are liquids at or near room temperature EXCEPT:
explanation: Beryllium is a solid metal at room temperature with a melting point of 1,287°C; gallium, caesium, and mercury are all liquids near room temperature.

title: What term is best associated with Sigmund Freud?
explanation: Sigmund Freud pioneered psychoanalysis, a therapeutic approach emphasizing unconscious processes and talk therapy to resolve psychological conflicts.

title: The humerus, paired radius, and ulna come together to form what joint?
explanation: The humerus, radius, and ulna articulate at the elbow joint, allowing flexion, extension, supination, and pronation movements.

title: What is the medical term for low blood sugar?
explanation: Hypoglycemia (blood glucose below 70 mg/dL) triggers shakiness, sweating, and confusion; severe cases cause seizures or loss of consciousness.

title: How many protons are in an oxygen atom?
explanation: Oxygen's atomic number is 8, meaning its nucleus contains eight protons, fundamental to its chemical properties and element identity.

title: Which of the following bones is not in the leg?
explanation: The radius is a forearm bone; all other options (patella, tibia, fibula) are bones located specifically in the leg or knee region.

title: What is an alternative name for multiple personality disorder?
explanation: Dissociative identity disorder (DID) involves two or more distinct personality states; it differs from schizophrenia, which is a psychotic disorder.

title: What is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere named?
explanation: The troposphere is Earth's lowest atmospheric layer (0-12 km altitude) where weather occurs and temperature decreases with altitude.

title: Which portion of the Marijuana plant produces the psychoactive substance known as THC?
explanation: Female marijuana flowers accumulate resin-rich trichomes containing THC and CBD; male flowers contain minimal THC, making females the primary source.

title: What is the same in Celsius and Fahrenheit?
explanation: Celsius and Fahrenheit scales intersect at -40 degrees; below this point, Celsius is lower, and above it, Celsius is higher.

title: Who is the chemical element Curium named after?
explanation: Curium (Cm, atomic number 96) was named in 1944 to honor Marie and Pierre Curie for their fundamental discoveries in radioactivity.

title: At what temperature does water boil?
explanation: Water boils at 212°F (100°C) at standard atmospheric pressure (101.325 kPa) at sea level.

title: Deuterium is an isotope of which element?
explanation: Deuterium is a stable isotope of hydrogen with one proton and one neutron; regular hydrogen has one proton and no neutrons.

title: What did Gregory Mendel use to test genetic crossovers?
explanation: Gregor Mendel used garden peas in his breeding experiments (1856-1863) to establish the fundamental laws of inheritance.

title: Gannymede is the largest moon of which planet?
explanation: Ganymede, Jupiter's largest moon, has a diameter of 5,268 km, making it larger than the planet Mercury.

title: All of the following programs are classified as raster graphics editors EXCEPT:
explanation: Inkscape is a vector graphics editor that uses mathematical curves and paths, while Paint.NET, GIMP, and Photoshop all work with pixel-based raster images.

title: While Apple was formed in California, in which western state was Microsoft founded?
explanation: Microsoft was founded in Albuquerque, New Mexico in 1975 before relocating to Washington state in 1979.

title: Which coding language was the #1 programming language in terms of usage on GitHub in 2015?
explanation: JavaScript dominated GitHub in 2015 with the highest number of repositories and pull requests across all programming languages.

title: HTML is what type of language?
explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is a markup language used to structure content, not a programming or scripting language.

title: The name of technology company HP stands for what?
explanation: HP stands for Hewlett-Packard, the company co-founded by William Hewlett and David Packard in 1939.

title: America Online (AOL) started out as which of these online service providers?
explanation: AOL evolved from Quantum Link, a service for Commodore 64 users that later became the commercial online service America Online.

title: Linus Torvalds created which of these?
explanation: Linus Torvalds created Linux in 1991 as a free Unix-like kernel, which became the foundation for many operating systems.

title: In computing, what does MIDI stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Musical Interface of Digital Instruments","Modular Interface of Digital Instruments","Musical Instrument Data Interface"}
explanation: MIDI is a protocol enabling digital instruments to communicate; it stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface.

title: What major programming language does Unreal Engine 4 use?
explanation: Unreal Engine 4 uses C++ as its primary programming language for game development and engine customization.

title: What was the first Android version specifically optimized for tablets?
explanation: Android Honeycomb (3.0) was the first version specifically designed and optimized for tablets in 2011.

title: What does SSD stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Solution Source Disk","Solid State Disk","Source Solution Drive"}
explanation: SSD stands for Solid State Drive, which uses flash memory instead of mechanical spinning disks for faster storage.

title: Lenovo acquired IBM's personal computer division, including the ThinkPad line of laptops and tablets, in what year?
explanation: Lenovo acquired IBM's personal computer division including ThinkPad in 2005 for $1.75 billion.

title: In networking, what does OSPF stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Order State Part First","Order Sense Ping Find","Open Signal Path Finder"}
explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a dynamic routing protocol that calculates paths using link-state algorithms.

title: The series of the Intel HD graphics generation succeeding that of the 5000 and 6000 series (Broadwell) is called:
explanation: Intel HD Graphics 500 succeeded the Broadwell-era 5000/6000 series with Skylake architecture in 2015.

title: What is the commonly used keyboard shortcut for the 'Copy' function on Windows OS?
explanation: Ctrl+C is the standard Windows keyboard shortcut for copying text or objects to the clipboard.

title: What amount of bits commonly equals one byte?
explanation: A byte consists of 8 bits, the fundamental unit of digital information in computing.

title: The Harvard architecture for micro-controllers added which additional bus?
explanation: Harvard architecture added a separate instruction bus alongside the data bus, enabling simultaneous access to instructions and data.

title: What internet protocol was documented in RFC 1459?
explanation: RFC 1459 documents the Internet Relay Chat (IRC) protocol, defining the standard for IRC client-server communication.

title: What kind of memory is used on memory cache?
explanation: SRAM (Static RAM) is used for CPU cache because it's fast but requires constant power and is expensive compared to DRAM.

title: In programming, what do you call functions with the same name but different implementations?
explanation: Overloading allows multiple functions with the same name but different parameter types or counts in the same scope.

title: What is largely considered the precursor to the USB format?
explanation: PS/2 connectors were the predecessor to USB, widely used for keyboards and mice before USB became standard.

title: What does the term USB stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Universal Simtex Blot","Unified Signal Bus","Unityped Semtex Backer"}
explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus, a standard interface for connecting peripherals to computers.

title: In the programming language Java, which of these keywords would you put on a variable to make sure it doesn't get modified?
explanation: The 'final' keyword in Java prevents a variable from being reassigned after initialization.

title: On which day did the World Wide Web go online?
explanation: The World Wide Web went online on December 20, 1990, when Tim Berners-Lee's HTTP server became publicly accessible.

title: Which of these names was an actual codename for a cancelled Microsoft project?
explanation: Neptune was a cancelled Microsoft project aimed at creating a thin-client web-based operating system in the late 1990s.

title: How long is an IPv6 address?
explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, providing vastly more address space than IPv4's 32-bit addresses.

title: What vulnerability ranked #1 on the OWASP Top 10 in 2013?
explanation: Injection attacks, including SQL injection and command injection, were ranked as the top OWASP vulnerability in 2013.

title: What does the DOS in Microsoft's first operating system "MS-DOS" stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Dumb Operating System","Driver Oriented System","Diskless Operating System"}
explanation: DOS stands for Disk Operating System, the text-based interface Microsoft used before Windows graphical shells.

title: Which internet company began life as an online bookstore called 'Cadabra'?
explanation: Amazon started as Cadabra, an online bookstore founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994, renaming to Amazon in 1995.

title: What does GHz stand for?
explanation: GHz is the abbreviation for Gigahertz, a unit of frequency equal to one billion cycles per second.

title: Approximately how many Apple I personal computers were created?
explanation: Apple I computers sold approximately 200 units at $666.66 each between 1976–1977 before the Apple II's release.

title: In computing, how many bits are in a nibble?
explanation: A nibble is 4 bits, half of a byte, commonly used in hexadecimal representation where each hex digit equals one nibble.

title: Which of the following is NOT a computer science algorithm?
explanation: Float Sort is not a recognized computer science algorithm; Bubble, Merge, and Quick Sort are all established sorting algorithms.

title: What was Bitcoin's block size limit in 2010?
explanation: Bitcoin's block size limit was set to 1 MB in 2010 as part of Satoshi Nakamoto's original design to prevent spam.

title: What is the most preferred image format used for logos in the Wikimedia database?
explanation: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is preferred for logos in Wikimedia because it's resolution-independent and compresses efficiently.

title: Released in 2001, the first edition of Apple's Mac OS X operating system (version 10.0) was given what animal code name?
explanation: Mac OS X 10.0 released in 2001 was codenamed Cheetah, beginning Apple's big-cat naming scheme for OS releases.

title: .at is the top-level domain for what country?
explanation: The .at top-level domain is assigned to Austria, derived from the country's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

title: Who is the original author of the realtime physics engine called PhysX?
explanation: NovodeX developed PhysX, the realtime physics engine that AGEIA later acquired and Nvidia eventually bought.

title: Which of the following is the oldest of these computers by release date?
explanation: The TRS-80 was released by Tandy in 1977, predating Commodore 64 (1982), ZX Spectrum (1982), and Apple III (1980).

title: Which data structure does FILO apply to?
explanation: FILO (First In Last Out) describes a Stack data structure where the most recently added element is removed first.

title: Which computer hardware device provides an interface for all other connected devices to communicate?
wrong_answers: {"Central Processing Unit","Hard Disk Drive","Random Access Memory"}
explanation: The motherboard provides the main circuit board connecting all hardware components through its buses and chipset.

title: Which kind of algorithm is Ron Rivest not famous for creating?
explanation: Ron Rivest is famous for RSA encryption, MD5 hashing, and RC4 stream cipher, but not for secret sharing schemes.

title: This mobile OS held the largest market share in 2012.
explanation: iOS held the largest mobile OS market share in 2012 with 27%, though Android was rapidly catching up.

title: The teapot often seen in many 3D modeling applications is called what?
explanation: The Utah Teapot is a standard 3D test model created at University of Utah in 1975, ubiquitous in graphics applications.

title: How fast is USB 3.1 Gen 2 theoretically?
explanation: USB 3.1 Gen 2 theoretically supports 10 Gb/s (gigabits per second), doubling Gen 1's 5 Gb/s speed.

title: Which of these Cherry MX mechanical keyboard switches is both tactile and clicky?
wrong_answers: {"Cherry MX Black","Cherry MX Red","Cherry MX Brown"}
explanation: Cherry MX Blue switches are both tactile (feedback bump) and clicky (audible click sound) when pressed.

title: According to the International System of Units, how many bytes are in a kilobyte of RAM?
explanation: The SI definition specifies 1 kilobyte equals 1000 bytes, though computing traditionally used 1024 (now called kibibyte).

title: What did the name of the Tor Anonymity Network orignially stand for?
wrong_answers: {"The Only Router","The Orange Router","The Ominous Router"}
explanation: Tor originally stood for The Onion Router, named for its layered encryption approach resembling an onion's rings.

title: Which RAID array type is associated with data mirroring?
explanation: RAID 1 implements mirroring, duplicating data across two drives for redundancy and read performance.

title: Dutch computer scientist Mark Overmars is known for creating which game development engine?
explanation: Mark Overmars created Game Maker at Université d'Amsterdam, which became a popular 2D game development tool.

title: Which of the following languages is used as a scripting language in the Unity 3D game engine?
explanation: Unity 3D uses C# as its primary scripting language for game logic and gameplay code.

title: Who is the founder of Palantir?
explanation: Peter Thiel co-founded Palantir Technologies in 2003 to develop big data analysis software.

title: What was the first commerically available computer processor?
explanation: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, was the first commercially available microprocessor with 2,300 transistors.

title: Which operating system was released first?
explanation: Mac OS was released in 1984, predating Windows (1985), Linux (1991), and OS/2 (1987).

title: What is the code name for the mobile operating system Android 7.0?
explanation: Android 7.0 released in 2016 was codenamed Nougat, continuing Google's dessert-based naming convention.

title: Generally, which component of a computer draws the most power?
explanation: Video cards (GPUs) typically consume the most power in modern computers, followed by processors and storage drives.

title: What does RAID stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Rapid Access for Indexed Devices","Range of Applications with Identical Designs","Randomized Abstract Identification Description"}
explanation: RAID stands for Redundant Array of Independent Disks, a technique for combining multiple drives for performance or reliability.

title: The programming language 'Swift' was created to replace what other programming language?
explanation: Swift was created by Apple in 2014 to gradually replace Objective-C for iOS, macOS, and system development.

title: On a standard American QWERTY keyboard, what symbol will you enter if you hold the shift key and press 1?
explanation: On a QWERTY keyboard, Shift+1 produces an exclamation mark (!), not dollar sign or other symbols.

title: In the programming language "Python", which of these statements would display the string "Hello World" correctly?
explanation: Python's print() function displays strings and objects; console.log is JavaScript, echo is Bash, printf is C.

title: Which one of these is not an official development name for a Ubuntu release?
explanation: Mystic Mansion is not an official Ubuntu release name; Ubuntu uses alliterative animal names like Jammy Jellyfish.

title: How many bits are commonly in a single byte?
explanation: A byte is defined as eight bits, the standard unit of digital storage and memory in computing.

title: What is the codename of the eighth generation Intel Core micro-architecture launched in October 2017?
explanation: Coffee Lake is Intel's eighth-generation Core processor architecture released in October 2017 with improved core counts.

title: What is the name of the process that sends one qubit of information using two bits of classical information?
explanation: Quantum teleportation transmits one qubit's state using two classical bits via entanglement and measurement.

title: What was the first company to use the term "Golden Master"?
explanation: Apple popularized the term 'Golden Master' to describe release-candidate software ready for manufacturing.

title: When did the online streaming service "Mixer" launch?
explanation: Mixer, Microsoft's streaming platform, launched in 2016 as a Twitch competitor before shutting down in 2020.

title: What does the term GPU stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Gaming Processor Unit","Graphite Producing Unit","Graphical Proprietary Unit"}
explanation: GPU stands for Graphics Processing Unit, a specialized processor designed for parallel computation and graphics rendering.

title: Which of these programming languages is a low-level language?
explanation: Assembly language is a low-level language with one-to-one correspondence to machine instructions, unlike Python/C#/Pascal.

title: What port does HTTP run on?
explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) runs on port 80, while HTTPS uses port 443 for encrypted connections.

title: In "Hexadecimal", what color would be displayed from the color code? "#00FF00"?
explanation: The hex color code #00FF00 produces green because the G channel (00FF) is maximum while R and B are zero.

title: Which of the following computer components can be built using only NAND gates?
explanation: An ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) can be constructed using only NAND gates, which are universal logic gates.

title: How many bits make up the significand portion of a single precision floating point number?
explanation: A single-precision (32-bit) float has a 23-bit significand (mantissa), with separate exponent and sign bits.

title: In computing, what does LAN stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Long Antenna Node","Light Access Node","Land Address Navigation"}
explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network, a computer network limited to a small geographic area like a building or campus.

title: Which of these is not a key value of Agile software development?
explanation: Comprehensive documentation contradicts Agile's emphasis on working software over documentation and responding to change.

title: What is the correct term for the metal object in between the CPU and the CPU fan within a computer system?
explanation: A heat sink is the metal component between the CPU and fan that dissipates heat through increased surface area.

title: In CSS, which of these values CANNOT be used with the "position" property?
explanation: The CSS position property accepts static, relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky, but 'center' is invalid for positioning.

title: The numbering system with a radix of 16 is more commonly referred to as
explanation: Hexadecimal (hex) is a base-16 numbering system using digits 0-9 and letters A-F for values 10-15.

title: What is the number of keys on a standard Windows Keyboard?
explanation: A standard Windows keyboard has 104 keys, including alphanumeric keys, function keys, and special function buttons.

title: What was the name of the security vulnerability found in Bash in 2014?
explanation: Shellshock was a critical Bash vulnerability discovered in 2014 allowing arbitrary code execution via environment variables.

title: How many Hz does the video standard PAL support?
explanation: PAL video standard supports 50 Hz refresh rate, while NTSC uses 60 Hz (or 59.94 Hz).

title: The internet domain .fm is the country-code top-level domain for which Pacific Ocean island nation?
explanation: The .fm domain is assigned to Micronesia (Federated States of Micronesia) under the ISO 3166-1 country code system.

title: In any programming language, what is the most common way to iterate through an array?
explanation: For loops are the most common and universal method for iterating through array elements across programming languages.

title: The computer OEM manufacturer Clevo, known for its Sager notebook line, is based in which country?
explanation: Clevo, maker of the Sager notebook brand, is based in Taiwan and supplies barebone systems to OEMs worldwide.

title: What does the "MP" stand for in MP3?
explanation: MP in MP3 stands for Moving Picture, derived from the MPEG (Moving Picture Experts Group) standard.

title: Australia, Japan, and Southeast Asia are in which ITU Region?
explanation: The ITU (International Telecommunication Union) divides the world into three regions; Region 3 covers Asia-Pacific.

title: What programming language was GitHub written in?
explanation: GitHub was originally written in Ruby on Rails before later components were developed in other languages.

title: What does the 'S' in the RSA encryption algorithm stand for?
explanation: RSA encryption was invented by Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman; the 'S' represents Adi Shamir.

title: Which of these people was NOT a founder of Apple Inc?
explanation: Jonathan Ive was Apple's Chief Design Officer but not a founder; Jobs, Wozniak, and Wayne founded Apple in 1976.

title: On which computer hardware device is the BIOS chip located?
wrong_answers: {"Hard Disk Drive","Central Processing Unit","Graphics Processing Unit"}
explanation: The BIOS chip is located on the motherboard and provides firmware for hardware initialization and boot processes.

title: Which computer language would you associate Django framework with?
explanation: Django is a web framework for Python, providing ORM, templating, and authentication utilities for rapid development.

title: What does the computer software acronym JVM stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Java Vendor Machine","Java Visual Machine","Just Virtual Machine"}
explanation: JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine, the runtime environment that interprets and executes compiled Java bytecode.

title: What was the name of the image that features as the default background wallpaper for Windows XP?
explanation: Bliss, a rolling hills landscape photo taken in Napa Valley, was Windows XP's iconic default desktop background.

title: What does CPU stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Central Process Unit","Computer Personal Unit","Central Processor Unit"}
explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the main processor executing instructions and performing computations.

title: Which of these is the name for the failed key escrow device introduced by the National Security Agency in 1993?
explanation: The Clipper Chip was an NSA-proposed encryption device using key escrow to allow government surveillance of communications.

title: The Windows OS was delevoped by which company?
explanation: Microsoft developed Windows, the dominant consumer operating system since the 1980s.

title: Moore's law originally stated that the number of transistors on a microprocessor chip would double every...
explanation: Moore's law originally stated transistor counts would double every year; this was later revised to every two years.

title: The Electron computer was released in Britain during 1983 for the home computing market, by which company?
explanation: Acorn Computers released the BBC Electron in 1983 as an affordable home computer in the UK market.

title: When Gmail first launched, how much storage did it provide for your email?
explanation: Gmail initially offered 1 GB of storage at launch in 2004, significantly more than the 25-50 MB offered by competitors.

title: Who invented the "Spanning Tree Protocol"?
explanation: Radia Perlman invented the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) in 1985, fundamental to modern network switching.

title: What is the name of the default theme that is installed with Windows XP?
explanation: Luna was Windows XP's default theme, featuring blue visual elements, and was the primary theme for the OS.

title: What is a polygon with eight sides called?
explanation: An octagon derives from the Greek prefix 'octo-' meaning eight, referring to any polygon with exactly eight sides and eight angles.

title: The French mathematician Évariste Galois is primarily known for his work in which?
wrong_answers: {"Galois' Continued Fractions","Galois' Method for PDE's","Abelian Integration"}
explanation: Galois Theory, developed from his work before his death at 20, provides a framework connecting polynomial equations to group structures and is fundamental to abstract algebra.

title: What shape does sin(x) or cos(x) make on a graph?
explanation: Sine and cosine functions produce smooth, repetitive oscillating curves characteristic of wave patterns due to their periodic nature and circular definition.

title: Who proved Fermat's Last Theorem?
explanation: Andrew Wiles completed the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 1995, using techniques from elliptic curves and modular forms after 358 years of being unsolved.

title: In Roman Numerals, what does XL equate to?
explanation: XL in Roman numerals represents 10 subtracted from 50 (L - X), which equals 40; subtractive notation was used for certain values to simplify representation.

title: How many square faces does a cube have?
explanation: A cube has 6 square faces: one on each side (top, bottom, front, back, left, right), making it a regular hexahedron.

title: How many books are in Euclid's Elements of Geometry?
explanation: Euclid's Elements is a 13-book compilation written around 300 BCE that systematically organized geometry, number theory, and other mathematical knowledge into logical proofs.

title: How many sides does a trapezium have?
explanation: A trapezium (trapezoid in US English) is defined as a quadrilateral with four sides, with at least one pair of parallel sides.

title: How many sides does a pentagon have?
explanation: The word pentagon comes from the Greek 'penta' meaning five and 'gon' meaning angle, denoting any polygon with exactly five sides.

title: Which of these numbers is closest to the total number of possible states for an army standard Enigma Machine?
explanation: The Enigma machine's rotor positions, plug board settings, and ring settings combine to create approximately 1.58 × 10²⁰ possible configurations.

title: What is the fourth digit of π?
explanation: Pi (π) begins as 3.14159..., so the digits after the decimal point are 1, 4, 1, making the fourth digit '1'.

title: Integration is the reverse of what mathematical operation?
explanation: Integration and differentiation are inverse operations; the derivative measures the rate of change while the integral finds the accumulated total.

title: The metric prefix "atto-" makes a measurement how much smaller than the base unit?
explanation: The SI prefix 'atto-' equals 10⁻¹⁸, making a measurement one quintillionth (10⁻¹⁸) of the base unit.

title: What's the square root of 49?
explanation: The square root of 49 is 7 because 7 × 7 = 49; it's the positive number that when multiplied by itself yields 49.

title: How many zeros are there in a googol?
explanation: A googol is 10¹⁰⁰, which is the digit 1 followed by 100 zeros, coined by Milton Sirotta, a mathematician's nine-year-old nephew.

title: Which mathematician refused the Fields Medal?
explanation: Grigori Perelman declined the Fields Medal in 2006 after proving the Poincaré conjecture, stating he rejected all prizes on principle.

title: What is the alphanumeric representation of the imaginary number?
explanation: The imaginary unit is represented by 'i', defined as the square root of -1, fundamental to complex number theory and electrical engineering.

title: What is the least number of sides a polygon can have?
explanation: A triangle is the polygon with the fewest sides (three), forming a closed shape; fewer sides cannot create a closed geometric polygon.

title: To the nearest whole number, how many radians are in a whole circle?
explanation: A complete circle contains 2π radians (approximately 6.28), which rounds to 6 when expressed to the nearest whole number.

title: What prime number comes next after 19?
explanation: 23 is the next prime number after 19, as 20, 21, and 22 are all divisible by numbers other than themselves and 1.

title: How many sides does a heptagon have?
explanation: A heptagon is a seven-sided polygon; the prefix 'hepta-' comes from Greek meaning seven, and '-gon' means angle or side.

title: What type of function is x²+2x+1?
explanation: The function x² + 2x + 1 is quadratic because it contains a second-degree term (x²) as its highest power.

title: What is the derivative of sin(x)
explanation: The derivative of sin(x) is cos(x), a fundamental calculus result showing the instantaneous rate of change of sine function equals cosine.

title: How many zeptometres are inside one femtometre?
explanation: One femtometer (10⁻¹⁵ m) equals one million zeptometers (10⁻²¹ m), as the difference in exponents is 10⁶.

title: What is the Roman numeral for 500?
explanation: The Roman numeral D represents 500; it derives from the Latin symbol for half of M (1000), originally written as Iↁ.

title: Which two men are credited with independently discovering differential calculus?
wrong_answers: {"Plato and Aristotle","Asiimov and Rutherford","Dvorak and Smith"}
explanation: Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz independently developed calculus in the late 17th century, sparking a historical priority dispute.

title: What is the only Millennium Prize Problem that has been solved so far?
explanation: The Poincaré conjecture (now a theorem) was solved by Grigori Perelman in 2002-2003, the only Millennium Prize Problem with a confirmed solution.

title: Which of the following famous mathematicians died in a duel at the age of 20?
explanation: Évariste Galois died in a duel at age 20 in 1832, likely over political views or a romantic dispute, the night before his execution.

title: What numbers are in the 5th row of Pascal's Triangle?
explanation: Pascal's Triangle row 5 (using 1-based indexing) is '1 4 6 4 1', the binomial coefficients from (a+b)⁴ expansion.

title: Which of these probability distributions is NOT discrete?
explanation: The normal (Gaussian) distribution is continuous, taking any real value, while binomial, Poisson, and hypergeometric distributions have discrete outcomes.

title: What is the name of a nine sided polygon?
explanation: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, derived from the Latin 'nona' meaning nine combined with the Greek '-gon' suffix for angle.

title: What is the area of a circle with a diameter of 20 inches if π= 3.1415?
explanation: For a circle with diameter 20 inches, the radius is 10; using A = πr², the area = 3.1415 × 100 = 314.15 square inches.

title: In the hexadecimal system, what number comes after 9?
explanation: Hexadecimal (base-16) uses digits 0-9 and letters A-F; after 9 comes A (representing 10 in decimal).

title: How many degrees make a full circle?
explanation: A full rotation is defined as 360 degrees, originating from ancient Babylonian astronomy and their base-60 numbering system.

title: How many Millibars (mbar) to 1 Inch of Mercury (inHg)
explanation: 1 inch of mercury = 33.9 millibars, a conversion factor based on the height of mercury in barometers at sea level.

title: The decimal number 31 in hexadecimal would be what?
explanation: The decimal 31 converts to 1F in hexadecimal: 1 × 16¹ + 15 × 16⁰ (where F = 15).

title: What comes after a Million, a Billion, and a Trillion?
explanation: The short scale order (used in English) progresses as million (10⁶), billion (10⁹), trillion (10¹²), then quadrillion (10¹⁵).

title: A mathematical constant, known as "The Golden Ratio", is most commonly represented by which greek letter?
explanation: Phi (Φ) represents the golden ratio (≈1.618), appearing throughout nature and geometry, often symbolized by the Greek letter Φ.

title: Which of the following mathematicians made major contributions to game theory?
explanation: John von Neumann pioneered game theory alongside Oskar Morgenstern, publishing the foundational work 'Theory of Games and Economic Behavior' (1944).

title: What Greek letter is used to signify summation?
explanation: The capital Greek letter sigma (Σ) is the standard mathematical symbol for summation of a sequence of numbers.

title: At what temperature does temp in °C equal temp in °F?
explanation: -40°C equals -40°F due to the formulas F = (C × 9/5) + 32; this is the unique temperature where both scales intersect.

title: What is the derivative of Acceleration with respect to time?
explanation: Jerk is the derivative of acceleration with respect to time, measuring the rate of change of acceleration in physics.

title: How many sides does a Möbius strip have?
explanation: A Möbius strip has only one side because it's a non-orientable surface created by twisting a rectangular strip 180 degrees before joining ends.

title: What is the mathematician Euler's first name?
explanation: Leonhard Euler (1707-1783), a prolific Swiss mathematician, made fundamental contributions across topology, graph theory, calculus, and numerous other fields.

title: What is the first Mersenne prime exponent over 1000?
explanation: 1279 is the first Mersenne prime exponent over 1000, meaning 2¹²⁷⁹ − 1 is prime; 2¹²⁷⁹ − 1 has 386 digits.

title: The Norse god Odin has two pet crows named "Huginn" and "Muninn". What do their names mean?
explanation: Huginn and Muninn mean 'Thought' and 'Memory' in Old Norse, serving as Odin's ravens who fly across the nine realms gathering information.

title: Who is the Egyptian god of reproduction and lettuce?
explanation: Min, an Egyptian fertility god with a tall plumed crown, was associated with reproduction and lettuces, which were believed to enhance virility.

title: Which of these mythological creatures is said to be half-man and half-horse?
explanation: A centaur is half-human, half-horse, a common figure in Greek mythology often depicted as wild and untamed, contrasting with civilized humans.

title: An Ankh is the Egyptian Hieroglyph for what?
explanation: The Ankh (☥) is an Egyptian symbol representing life, used in hieroglyphics and worn as an amulet; it combines a cross and oval loop.

title: Which Norse God has a horse named Sleipnir?
explanation: Odin, the All-Father in Norse mythology, rides Sleipnir, an eight-legged horse capable of traveling between the nine realms.

title: In Greek Mythology, who killed Achilles?
explanation: Paris of Troy killed Achilles by shooting an arrow into his heel (his only vulnerable point) during the Trojan War.

title: The ancient Roman god of war was commonly known as which of the following?
explanation: Mars was the Roman god of war, equivalent to the Greek god Ares; the planet Mars is named after him.

title: According to Algonquian folklore, how does one transform into a Wendigo?
wrong_answers: {"Excessive mutilation of animal corpses.","Performing a ritual involving murder.","Drinking the blood of many slain animals."}
explanation: In Algonquian folklore, cannibalism transforms a person into a Wendigo, a cannibalistic spirit condemned to eternally hunger for human flesh.

title: The Nike apparel and footwear brand takes it's name from the Greek goddess of what?
explanation: Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, lends her name to the sports brand; her symbol (a winged figure) appears in the Nike logo.

title: This Greek goddess's name was chosen for the dwarf planet responsible for discord on Pluto's classification amongst astronomers.
explanation: Eris, the Greek goddess of discord, was chosen as the name for the dwarf planet because its discovery caused 'discord' over Pluto's classification.

title: Who was the King of Gods in Ancient Greek mythology?
explanation: Zeus ruled as king of the Greek gods and the sky, residing on Mount Olympus; his siblings were Poseidon and Hades.

title: Who did Hippomenes defeat in a footrace?
explanation: Hippomenes defeated the swift runner Atalanta in a footrace by dropping golden apples during the race, distracting her.

title: The greek god Poseidon was the god of what?
explanation: Poseidon, one of the twelve Olympian gods, controlled the oceans, earthquakes, and storms in Greek mythology.

title: Hera is god of...
explanation: Hera, queen of the gods and wife of Zeus, presided over marriage, women, and family in Greek mythology.

title: In Norse Mythology, what is the name of the symbol commonly referred to as the "Tree of Life"?
explanation: Yggdrasil is the World Tree in Norse mythology, whose roots and branches connect the nine realms and support all existence.

title: How many heads does Cerberus have?
explanation: Cerberus, the three-headed dog of the underworld, guarded the gates of Hades in Greek mythology, preventing the dead from leaving.

title: What is the name of the Greek god of blacksmiths?
explanation: Hephaestus, the Greek god of blacksmiths and metalworking, was often depicted with a hammer and anvil in mythological artwork.

title: Who was the Roman god of fire?
explanation: Vulcan, the Roman god of fire and metalworking, is equivalent to the Greek god Hephaestus and gives his name to volcanoes.

title: The Maori hold that which island nation was founded by Kupe, who discovered it under a long white cloud?
explanation: According to Maori legend, Kupe discovered Aotearoa (New Zealand) and described it as 'Aotearoa' meaning 'the land of the long white cloud'.

title: A minotaur is half human half what?
explanation: The Minotaur in Greek mythology was half-human, half-bull, imprisoned in Crete's labyrinth, slain by the hero Theseus.

title: In Norse mythology, what is the name of the serpent which eats the roots of the ash tree Yggdrasil?
explanation: Nidhogg is a serpent in Norse mythology that constantly gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil, the World Tree.

title: In Greek Mythology, who was the daughter of King Minos?
explanation: Ariadne, daughter of King Minos of Crete, helped Theseus navigate the Minotaur's labyrinth by providing him a ball of thread.

title: What immense structure is referred to in Norse Mythology as the Yggdrasil.
explanation: Yggdrasil is the immense cosmic tree in Norse mythology whose branches and roots interconnect the nine realms of existence.

title: In Norse Mythology, Baldr was killed by Loki with a magical spear made from what plant?
explanation: In Norse mythology, Loki killed Baldr with a spear made from mistletoe, the only substance capable of harming the otherwise invulnerable god.

title: Which Greek & Roman god was known as the god of music, truth and prophecy, healing, the sun and light, plague, poetry, and more?
explanation: Apollo, a major Olympian deity, was revered as god of music, truth, prophecy, healing, the sun, plague, and poetry among many domains.

title: Talos, the mythical giant bronze man, was the protector of which island?
explanation: Talos, a bronze guardian automaton, protected Crete in Greek mythology by patrolling its shores and destroying invaders.

title: According to Japanese folklore, what is the favorite food of the Kappa.
explanation: In Japanese folklore, Kappa are water creatures with a strong preference for cucumbers, making them an effective lure or appeasement offering.

title: This Greek mythological figure is the god/goddess of battle strategy (among other things).
explanation: Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom, strategy, and warfare, represented the intellectual and tactical aspects of battle.

title: What mythology did the god "Apollo" come from?
wrong_answers: {"Roman and Spanish","Greek and Chinese","Greek, Roman and Norse"}
explanation: Apollo appears in both Greek and Roman mythology, retaining the same name and characteristics across both cultures.

title: Nidhogg is a mythical creature from what mythology?
explanation: Nidhogg originates from Norse mythology, appearing in the Norse creation myth as the serpent gnawing Yggdrasil's roots.

title: Which of the following is not one of the Greek Fates?
explanation: Narcissus was a beautiful human mortal in Greek mythology, not one of the three Fates (Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos).

title: Which of the following Mesopotamian mythological figures was NOT a deity?
explanation: Enkidu was a wild man created by the gods in Mesopotamian mythology, not a deity himself, though other figures listed were gods.

title: What is the name of the wildman that Gilgamesh befriends and goes on adventures with?
explanation: Enkidu is the wildman and companion of Gilgamesh in the ancient Mesopotamian epic, created to counter Gilgamesh's tyranny.

title: Who in Greek mythology, who led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece?
explanation: Jason led the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece, one of the most famous adventures in Greek mythology.

title: According to the Egyptian Myth of Osiris, who murdered Osiris?
explanation: In Egyptian mythology, Set (also called Seth) murdered his brother Osiris by trapping him in a coffin, beginning Osiris' underworld reign.

title: In most traditions, who was the wife of Zeus?
explanation: Hera was the principal wife and queen consort of Zeus in Greek mythology, goddess of marriage and family.

title: Who was the only god from Greece who did not get a name change in Rome?
explanation: Apollo is the only Greek Olympian deity who retained his name unchanged when adopted into Roman mythology.

title: Hel was the daughter of which Norse Mythological figure?
explanation: In Norse mythology, Hel, goddess of the underworld, is the daughter of Loki, the trickster god.

title: Which figure from Greek mythology traveled to the underworld to return his wife Eurydice to the land of the living?
explanation: Orpheus traveled to the underworld to retrieve his deceased wife Eurydice, nearly succeeding before a fatal glance backward.

title: Which of these Roman gods doesn't have a counterpart in Greek mythology?
explanation: Janus, the Roman god of beginnings and endings represented by a two-faced figure, has no direct Greek mythological counterpart.

title: What weakpoint of Achilles was expoited by the Trojan prince, Paris?
explanation: Achilles' only vulnerability was his heel, where his mother Thetis held him while dipping him in the River Styx; Paris exploited this weakness.

title: What is the name of the first human being in Norse mythology?
explanation: Ask (also called Askr) was the first human created in Norse mythology, formed from an ash tree by Odin and his brothers.

title: What mytological creatures have women's faces and vultures' bodies?
explanation: Harpies in Greek mythology were female creatures with women's heads and torsos but wings and bodies of vultures, known for theft and defilement.

title: Who is a minor god that is protector and creator of various arts, such as cheese making and bee keeping.
explanation: Aristaeus was a minor Greek god credited with protecting and inventing various crafts including cheese making and bee keeping.

title: Which greek god/goddess tossed a golden apple with the words "for the fairest" into the middle of the feast of the gods?
explanation: Eris, the goddess of discord, tossed the golden apple inscribed 'for the fairest' into the gods' feast, sparking the Trojan War.

title: What is the name of the Greek god of peaceful deaths?
explanation: Thanatos was the personification of peaceful, natural death in Greek mythology, distinct from violent death represented by Ares.

title: Neptune's greek name was...
explanation: Poseidon, the Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and storms, was given the Roman name Neptune.

title: What is the capital of Indonesia?
explanation: Jakarta, Indonesia's capital since 1945, is located on Java island and serves as the country's political, economic, and cultural center.

title: What continent is the country Lesotho in?
explanation: Lesotho is an entirely landlocked country completely surrounded by South Africa on the African continent.

title: Which is the largest of these 4 islands?
explanation: Borneo at 748,168 km² is larger than Great Britain (242,495 km²), Cuba (109,884 km²), and Madagascar (587,041 km²).

title: What is the capital of Denmark?
explanation: Copenhagen, Denmark's capital since the early 12th century, is located on the island of Zealand and Amager.

title: What is the Capital of the United States?
wrong_answers: {"Los Angelas, CA","New York City, NY","Houston, TX"}
explanation: Washington, D.C. has been the capital of the United States since 1800, purpose-built as a compromise between northern and southern states.

title: What is the capital of Spain?
explanation: Madrid, located in central Spain, has been the capital since 1561 when Philip II moved the court there from Toledo.

title: Bir Tawil, an uninhabited track of land claimed by no country, is located along the border of which two countries?
wrong_answers: {"Israel and Jordan","Chad and Libya","Iraq and Saudi Arabia"}
explanation: Bir Tawil, a disputed 2,060 km² area between Egypt and Sudan, is unclaimed because both countries prefer the other's border interpretation.

title: The Alps are a mountain range on which continent?
explanation: The Alps stretch across eight countries in Europe, forming the continent's longest mountain range with peaks exceeding 4,800 meters.

title: What is the second-largest city in Lithuania?
explanation: Kaunas is Lithuania's second-most populous city after the capital Vilnius, serving as the historic cultural and economic center during the interwar period.

title: What city is known as the Rose Capital of the World?
explanation: Tyler, Texas earned this title due to its ideal climate for rose cultivation and the annual Rose Festival first held in 1933, making it the world's leading producer of rose bushes.

title: What is special about Lake Titicaca?
wrong_answers: {"Longest lake in the world","Deepest lake in the world","Remains frozen all year round"}
explanation: At 3,812 meters elevation, Lake Titicaca is the highest lake in the world on which commercial vessels operate, shared between Peru and Bolivia.

title: The Gambia is a nation found on which continent?
explanation: The Gambia is a West African nation bordered by Senegal, located in a narrow strip along the Gambia River on the Atlantic coast.

title: How many counties in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation: The Republic of Ireland comprises 26 counties; the additional 6 counties in Northern Ireland are part of the United Kingdom.

title: In which English county is Stonehenge?
explanation: Stonehenge sits on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, approximately 9 miles north of the town of Salisbury in southwestern England.

title: What North American tourist attraction is served by the "Maid of the Mist" tour company?
explanation: The Maid of the Mist has been operating boat tours at Niagara Falls since 1846, carrying tourists beneath the cascading waters on both the Canadian and American sides.

title: What country has a horizontal bicolor red and white flag?
explanation: Monaco's flag features two equal horizontal stripes of red and white, adopted officially in 1881 as the national standard.

title: Which of these Japanese islands is the largest by area?
explanation: Shikoku, the smallest of Japan's four main islands, covers approximately 18,800 km² and is larger than Okinawa Prefecture by total area.

title: In Washington, D.C. what does the "C" stand for?
explanation: Washington, District of Columbia was named after President George Washington; Columbia derives from Christopher Columbus and represents the nation's identity in formal naming.

title: Where is the city of Haarlem located?
explanation: Haarlem is a historic city in the province of North Holland in the western Netherlands, located approximately 20 km west of Amsterdam.

title: Where is Fort Marlborough located?
explanation: Fort Marlborough is a British colonial fortress built in 1685, located in Bengkulu on the island of Sumatra in Indonesia.

title: How many federal states does Germany have?
explanation: Germany is organized into 16 federal states called Länder, a structure established after reunification in 1990.

title: Which country claims ownership of the disputed state Kosovo?
explanation: Serbia officially claims sovereignty over Kosovo, though Kosovo declared independence in 2008; Serbia does not recognize this declaration.

title: Which of the following countries does NOT recognize Armenia as an independent country?
explanation: Pakistan is one of the few countries that does not recognize Armenia's independence, maintaining this stance due to historical and geopolitical tensions.

title: Bikini Atoll is in which country?
explanation: Bikini Atoll is part of the Marshall Islands, a Pacific island nation that became independent from U.S. trusteeship in 1986.

title: Which country is the home of the largest Japanese population outside of Japan?
explanation: Brazil hosts over 2 million people of Japanese descent, the largest diaspora community resulting from 20th-century immigration patterns.

title: A lion brandishing a sword is depicted on the national flag of which country?
explanation: Sri Lanka's flag features a golden lion holding an upraised sword, symbolizing courage and sovereignty, centered in the national design.

title: What is the land connecting North America and South America?
explanation: The Isthmus of Panama forms the narrow land bridge connecting the North and South American continents, spanning approximately 80 kilometers.

title: Harvard University is located in which city?
explanation: Harvard University is located in Cambridge, Massachusetts, across the Charles River from Boston, where it was founded in 1636.

title: What country is not a part of Scandinavia?
explanation: Finland is not geographically part of Scandinavia, though it shares Nordic heritage; Scandinavia comprises Norway, Sweden, and Denmark.

title: The Svalbard Archipelago is a dependency of which country?
explanation: Svalbard is an Arctic archipelago and Norwegian territory, administered by Norway since 1920 under the Svalbard Treaty.

title: Which of the following languages does NOT use the Latin alphabet?
explanation: Georgian uses its own unique alphabet (Georgian script) developed in the 5th century, distinct from Latin, Cyrillic, or Arabic scripts.

title: What is the name of the Canadian national anthem?
wrong_answers: {"O Red Maple","Leaf-Spangled Banner","March of the Puck Drop"}
explanation: O Canada was officially adopted as the national anthem in 1980, replacing God Save the Queen, with French and English versions of equal standing.

title: Which of these countries is not a United Nations member state?
explanation: Niue is a self-governing state in free association with New Zealand but is not a UN member state; it maintains observer status instead.

title: What is the name of the peninsula containing Spain and Portugal?
explanation: The Iberian Peninsula is bounded by the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea, encompassing Spain and Portugal in southwestern Europe.

title: What is the northernmost human settlement with year round inhabitants?
explanation: Alert, Canada, at 82.5°N latitude, is the northernmost continuously inhabited settlement in the world with permanent residents.

title: Where is the ancient city of Petra located?
explanation: Petra, an ancient Nabataean city carved from rose-colored stone, is located in southwestern Jordan near the Dead Sea.

title: Which of these island countries is located in the Caribbean?
explanation: Barbados is an island nation in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean, located northeast of Venezuela.

title: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of which country?
explanation: Kuala Lumpur, meaning "muddy confluence" in Malay, is the capital and largest city of Malaysia, situated in the Klang Valley.

title: What is the capital city of Slovenia?
explanation: Ljubljana has been Slovenia's capital since independence in 1991, serving as the country's cultural, economic, and political center.

explanation: Kyrgyzstan shares borders with 4 countries: Kazakhstan, China, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, making it a key geographic hub in Central Asia.

title: The Principality of Sealand is an unrecognized micronation off the coast of what country?
explanation: Sealand is a micronation located on an artificial platform (Roughs Tower) off the coast of Essex in the United Kingdom.

title: In which city is the Big Nickel located in Canada?
explanation: The Big Nickel is located in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada, a giant replica of a Canadian nickel coin honoring the region's mining heritage.

title: The country of Belize borders which country?
explanation: Belize borders Guatemala to the west and south, with which it shares a disputed territory; it also borders Mexico to the north.

title: The derisive acronym "PIIGS" refers to which of the following European countries and their economic statuses?
wrong_answers: {"Poland, Iceland, Italy, Greece, Serbia","Poland, Iceland, Italy, Greenland, Spain","Portugal, Iceland, Ireland, Greece, Serbia"}
explanation: PIIGS stands for Portugal, Ireland, Italy, Greece, and Spain, countries heavily impacted by the 2008 financial crisis and European debt crisis.

title: Which Russian oblast forms a border with Poland?
explanation: Kaliningrad is a Russian enclave bordering Poland to the west, separated from mainland Russia and surrounded by EU and NATO members.

title: The body of the Egyptian Sphinx was based on which animal?
explanation: The Great Sphinx of Giza has a lion's body, representing strength and royalty in ancient Egyptian culture and serving as a guardian figure.

title: What is the largest non-continental island in the world?
explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island at 2.166 million km², though it remains a dependent territory of Denmark rather than an independent nation.

title: In what part of Wales will you find the village Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch?
explanation: This notoriously long Welsh village name (meaning "Church of Mary in the hollow of white hazel") is located on the island of Anglesey off the northwest coast.

title: What is the state capital of South Dakota?
explanation: Pierre became South Dakota's capital in 1875 despite being smaller than cities like Sioux Falls; it was chosen as a central location on the Missouri River.

title: On which continent is the country of Angola located?
explanation: Angola is located in south-central Africa and was a Portuguese colony until gaining independence in 1975.

title: What tiny principality lies between Spain and France?
explanation: Andorra sits in the Pyrenees between Spain and France with a unique co-principality system under joint rule by a Spanish bishop and French count.

title: All of the following are classified as Finno-Ugric languages EXCEPT:
explanation: Samoyedic languages form a separate Uralic branch; Hungarian, Finnish, and Estonian are Finno-Ugric languages within the same family.

title: About how many countries are there in the world?
explanation: The United Nations currently recognizes 193 UN member states plus 2 observer states (Vatican and Palestine), totaling approximately 197 sovereign territories.

title: Which of these cities is NOT in England?
explanation: Edinburgh is Scotland's capital, located north of the border, while Oxford, Manchester, and Southampton are all English cities.

title: Where is the fast food chain "Panda Express" headquartered?
explanation: Panda Express was founded in 1983 and is headquartered in Rosemead, California, a city in Los Angeles County.

title: When does Finland celebrate their independence day?
explanation: Finland's independence day commemorates December 6, 1917, when the nation declared independence from the Russian Empire.

title: Which country is the Taedong River in?
explanation: The Taedong River flows through North Korea and is a historically important waterway that runs through Pyongyang.

title: Which of these is NOT a city in India?
explanation: Islamabad is Pakistan's capital; Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, and Ghaziabad are all major cities within India's borders.

title: Which country ranks first in the number of historically active volcanoes?
explanation: Indonesia has approximately 130 historically active volcanoes spread across its archipelago due to its position on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

title: What event led to Liechenstein adding a crown to its flag?
wrong_answers: {"Coronation of Prince Johann I Joseph in 1805","Charles VI's decree in 1719","Signing of the 1862 Constitution of Liechtenstein"}
explanation: The 1936 Berlin Olympics highlighted the confusion between Liechtenstein and Haiti's nearly identical flags, prompting Liechtenstein to add a crown to distinguish itself.

title: Which Borough is the farthest in the north of New York City?
explanation: The Bronx extends farthest north among NYC's five boroughs, with its northern boundary at the Westchester County line.

title: Which of the following Arab countries does NOT have a flag containing only Pan-Arab colours?
explanation: Qatar's flag features white and maroon, while other Gulf nations use the Pan-Arab colors of red, white, black, and green.

title: How many countries share a land border with Luxembourg?
explanation: Luxembourg shares land borders with Belgium, France, and Germany—three distinct countries across its modest 2,586 km² territory.

title: What is the capital of the US State of New York?
explanation: Albany has been New York's state capital since 1797, though New York City is the largest city and capital of commerce.

title: The Hunua Ranges is located in...
explanation: The Hunua Ranges form a forest ecosystem in the North Island of New Zealand, southeast of Auckland.

title: How many countries are larger than Australia?
explanation: Only Russia, Canada, USA, China, and Brazil exceed Australia's 7.69 million km² in total area.

title: What is the capital of Finland?
explanation: Helsinki became Finland's capital in 1812 when the Russian Empire transferred it from Turku to strengthen control of the Swedish-speaking region.

title: Which nation claims ownership of Antarctica?
correct_answer: No one, but there are claims.
explanation: Antarctica is governed by the Antarctic Treaty System (1961), which suspends all territorial claims and designates it as a scientific preserve.

title: What is the name of the former country that was succeeded by countries such as Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia?
explanation: Yugoslavia dissolved in the 1990s, with Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia emerging as successor states.

title: Which of the following countries has a flag featuring a yellow lion wielding a sword on a dark red background?
explanation: Sri Lanka's flag features the Lion Flag with a yellow lion holding a scimitar on a deep red background, a symbol of Sinhalese sovereignty.

title: What is the capital of South Korea?
explanation: Seoul has been South Korea's capital and largest city since the nation's founding, serving as the political and economic center.

title: Which of the following countries banned the use of personal genetic ancestry tests?
explanation: Germany prohibits direct-to-consumer genetic ancestry testing to protect privacy and prevent genetic discrimination under its strict data protection laws.

title: Which of these African countries displays a gun on their flag?
explanation: Mozambique's flag uniquely features an AK-47 rifle crossed with a machete, symbolizing the nation's armed struggle for independence from Portugal.

title: What is the fifth largest country by area?
explanation: Brazil ranks fifth by area at 8.515 million km² after Russia, Canada, USA, and China.

title: With which country does France share its largest land border
explanation: France shares its longest land border with Brazil (via French Guiana), spanning roughly 730 km along the Oiapoque River.

title: What is the capital of Jamaica?
explanation: Kingston became Jamaica's capital in 1872, replacing Spanish Town as the seat of government and primary port city.

title: Which of these is NOT a real tectonic plate?
explanation: The Atlantic Plate does not exist; the Atlantic Ocean's seafloor is part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the North American and Eurasian plates diverge.

title: Which of these is NOT a province in China?
explanation: Yangtze is a river, not a province; Fujian, Sichuan, and Guangdong are all actual provinces of China.

title: Where is the Volga River?
explanation: The Volga is Europe's longest river at 3,530 km, flowing through western Russia from the Valdai Hills to the Caspian Sea.

title: What is the capital of Slovakia?
explanation: Bratislava sits on the Danube River and has been Slovakia's capital since the country's independence in 1993.

title: What is the capital city of New Zealand?
explanation: Wellington, located at the southern tip of the North Island, became New Zealand's capital in 1865, replacing Auckland.

title: The historical city Timbuktu is located in which West African country?
explanation: Timbuktu flourished as a major Mali trading center and Islamic learning hub from the 12th century onward on the Niger River.

title: Which is the world's longest river?
explanation: The Nile River spans 6,650 km through northeastern Africa, making it the world's longest river by a narrow margin over the Amazon.

title: What is the Finnish word for "Finland"?
explanation: "Suomi" is Finland's native name for itself, derived from ancient Germanic and Uralic roots meaning "land of swamps."

title: What is the most populous Muslim-majority nation in 2010?
explanation: Indonesia's Muslim population exceeded 200 million by 2010, making it the world's largest Muslim-majority nation by total population.

title: Which river was dammed to create Gatun Lake and the Panama Canal?
explanation: The Chagres River was dammed to create Gatun Lake in 1907, which supplies fresh water and raises ships between the Atlantic and Pacific.

title: The Space Needle is located in which city?
explanation: The Space Needle was built for Seattle's 1962 World's Fair and remains the city's most iconic landmark at 605 feet tall.

title: The land of Gotland is located in which European country?
explanation: Gotland is a large Swedish island in the Baltic Sea known for its medieval heritage and distinct cultural identity.

title: What is the capital of Romania?
explanation: Bucharest became Romania's capital in 1862 and grew into a major Balkan city, though much was rebuilt after World War II.

title: The formerly East-Prussian city of Königsberg is known as which Russian City today?
explanation: Königsberg was renamed Kaliningrad in 1946 after the Soviet Union annexed the East Prussian city following World War II.

title: What is the largest country, by area, that has only one time zone?
explanation: China spans five geographic time zones but officially uses a single time zone (China Standard Time) across the entire nation.

title: Which city is the biggest in Canada?
explanation: Toronto became Canada's largest city by population, surpassing Montreal in the late 20th century with its booming economy and immigration.

title: What is the largest lake in the African continent?
explanation: Lake Victoria spans 68,870 km² across Uganda, Tanzania, and Kenya, making it Africa's largest lake by surface area.

title: How many sovereign states are members of the United Nations?
explanation: The UN has 193 member states plus 2 observer states (Vatican and Palestine), totaling 195 sovereign entities in the system.

title: Which of these is an official currency of the Cook Islands?
explanation: The Cook Islands, an autonomous state in free association with New Zealand, uses both the Cook Islands Dollar and New Zealand Dollar.

title: What is the capital of Seychelles?
explanation: Victoria, capital of the Seychelles archipelago, is located on Mahé island and serves as the nation's main administrative and port hub.

title: Which of these is NOT an island that is part of the Philippines?
explanation: Java is part of Indonesia, not the Philippines; Luzon, Mindanao, and Palawan are all major Philippine islands.

title: Which of these cities has a 4° East longitude.
explanation: Amsterdam sits at approximately 4°52'E longitude, the closest of the listed cities to the prime meridian reference point.

title: What island in the Canary Islands was the scene of one of the worst air disasters in history with the collision of two jumbo jets?
explanation: The 1977 Tenerife airport disaster killed 583 people when two Boeing 747s collided, the deadliest aviation accident in history.

title: The mountainous Khyber Pass connects which of the two following countries?
wrong_answers: {"India and Nepal","Pakistan and India","Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan"}
explanation: The Khyber Pass is a historic mountain pass through the Hindu Kush connecting Peshawar, Pakistan with Kabul, Afghanistan.

title: What is Canada's largest island?
explanation: Baffin Island covers 507,451 km² in the Canadian Arctic, making it North America's second-largest island after Greenland.

title: What African country has Portuguese as its official language?
explanation: Mozambique inherited Portuguese as its official language from colonial rule ending in 1975, unlike most nearby African nations.

title: What is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka?
explanation: Colombo is Sri Lanka's largest city and commercial center, though Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the administrative capital.

title: Which of these countries is the smallest by population?
explanation: Norway's population of roughly 5.5 million is smaller than Slovakia (5.8M), Finland (5.5M is close), and Hong Kong (7.6M).

title: What is the name of the ocean that Hawaii is located in?
explanation: Hawaii is located in the North Pacific Ocean, making it part of Polynesia and the United States' only insular state.

title: Which of these places is a location in Cornwall?
explanation: Barcelona, known as "the Barcelona of Cornwall," is a small village on Cornwall's south coast famous for its sandy beach.

title: Greenland is a part of which kingdom?
explanation: Greenland is a constituent country within the Kingdom of Denmark, maintaining home rule with defense and foreign affairs handled by Denmark.

title: On which continent does the Andes mountain range lie?
explanation: The Andes mountain range runs along the western edge of South America, stretching from Colombia to southern Chile.

title: Which islands below have been claimed by both Japan and Russia?
explanation: The Kuril Islands remain disputed between Japan and Russia, with Japan claiming the southern islands (Iturup, Kunashir, Shikotan, Habomai).

title: Which of these is the name of the largest city in the US state Tennessee?
explanation: Memphis is Tennessee's largest city by population, named after the ancient Egyptian capital and known for music and cultural history.

title: Which of the following former Yugoslavian states is landlocked?
explanation: Serbia is landlocked after Yugoslavia's breakup, while Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Croatia all have Adriatic coastlines.

title: Which is the smallest country in the world?
explanation: Vatican City covers just 0.44 km² and is the smallest independent state by both area and population (under 1,000).

title: Which stretch of water connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea?
explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar is the narrow waterway separating Spain from Morocco, connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.

title: What name was historically used for the Turkish city currently known as Istanbul?
explanation: Constantinople was renamed Istanbul in 1930 following Turkey's transition from Ottoman to modern secular governance.

title: Bridgetown is the capital of which island country in the Carribean?
explanation: Barbados, located at the eastern edge of the Caribbean, gained independence in 1966 and Bridgetown serves as its capital.

title: Which of the following geographic features is a ring-shaped coral reef, island, or series of islets?
explanation: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island or reef enclosing a lagoon, typically found in tropical oceans and formed by coral growth around a subsiding volcano.

title: What is the capital of Lithuania?
explanation: Vilnius became Lithuania's capital in 1323 and remains the nation's largest city and cultural heart.

title: What is the capital of Chile?
explanation: Santiago sits in the central valley at the foot of the Andes and has been Chile's capital since the nation's independence in 1818.

title: How many countries does the United States share a land border with?
explanation: The United States shares land borders with Canada to the north and Mexico to the south, totaling two nations.

title: The land mass of modern day Turkey is called what?
explanation: Anatolia, also known as Asia Minor, comprises the peninsula that forms the majority of modern-day Turkey's territory.

title: The Maluku islands (informally known as the Spice Islands) belong to which country?
explanation: The Maluku Islands were historically called the Spice Islands and are part of Indonesia, known for their valuable clove and nutmeg production.

title: What is Canada's smallest province?
explanation: Prince Edward Island at 5,660 km² is Canada's smallest province, located in the Atlantic Ocean east of Nova Scotia.

title: Which of these countries is not written in its native language?
explanation: Slovaško means "Slovak" (the language/nationality) rather than being Slovakia's native name; Suomi (Finland), Schweiz (Switzerland), and Elláda (Greece) are native names.

title: What is Russia's second-largest city?
explanation: Saint Petersburg, Russia's cultural capital on the Baltic Sea, is the second-largest city by population after Moscow.

title: What is the name of one of the Neo-Aramaic languages spoken by the Jewish population from Northwestern Iraq?
explanation: Lishana Deni is a Jewish Neo-Aramaic language spoken by communities from the Dena region of northwestern Iraq.

title: Which of these countries is NOT a part of the Asian continent?
explanation: Suriname is located in South America on the northern coast; Georgia and Russia are transcontinental, and Singapore is in Southeast Asia.

title: In which English county is the city of Portsmouth?
explanation: Portsmouth is located in Hampshire county on England's south coast, serving as a historic naval port on the English Channel.

title: How many stars are featured on New Zealand's flag?
explanation: New Zealand's flag features four red five-pointed stars representing the Southern Cross constellation visible from the Southern Hemisphere.

title: The Suez Canal is located in which African country?
explanation: The Suez Canal, built through Egypt in 1869, connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and is critical for global maritime trade.

title: How many countries are inside the United Kingdom?
explanation: The United Kingdom comprises four constituent countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

title: Which of these is NOT a city in Saudi Arabia?
explanation: Dubai is located in the United Arab Emirates, not Saudi Arabia; Riyadh, Mecca, and Medina are all Saudi Arabian cities.

title: What was the most populous city in the Americas in 2015?
explanation: São Paulo's metropolitan area exceeded 20 million people by 2015, surpassing New York, Mexico City, and Los Angeles.

title: Which of these countries is NOT the only country to start with that letter of the alphabet?
explanation: Zambia is not the only country starting with Z (Zimbabwe also exists), while Qatar, Yemen, and Oman are each the sole nations beginning with their letter.

title: What is the region conjoining Pakistan, India, and China with unknown leadership called?
explanation: Kashmir is a disputed region whose governance is contested by Pakistan, India, and China, with portions controlled by each.

title: Which of the following European languages is classified as a "language isolate?"
explanation: Basque is a language isolate unrelated to any other European language family, spoken in the Basque Country region of Spain and France.

title: What is the most common climbing route for the second highest mountain in the world, K2?
explanation: The Abruzzi Spur is the most frequently used route on K2 due to its relatively safer passage compared to other technical approaches.

title: How many provinces are in the Netherlands?
