explanation: The Netherlands has 12 provinces: Groningen, Friesland, Drenthe, Overijssel, Flevoland, Gelderland, Utrecht, North Holland, South Holland, Zeeland, North Brabant, and Limburg.

title: What is the capital city of Bermuda?
explanation: Hamilton has been Bermuda's capital since 1815 and is located on the island of Bermuda in the Atlantic Ocean east of North America.

title: In which war did the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki occur?
explanation: The atomic bombings of Hiroshima (August 6) and Nagasaki (August 9, 1945) occurred in the final weeks of World War II in the Pacific Theater.

title: What is the oldest US state?
explanation: Delaware ratified the U.S. Constitution on December 7, 1787, becoming the first state and earning the title "First State."

title: Against which country did the Dutch Republic fight the Eighty Years' War?
explanation: The Eighty Years' War (1568-1648) was the Dutch Republic's struggle for independence against Spanish rule, ending with the Treaty of Münster.

title: What is the name of the US Navy spy ship which was attacked and captured by North Korean forces in 1968?
explanation: The USS Pueblo was seized by North Korea in January 1968; the ship and its crew were eventually released but the vessel remains in North Korea.

title: The United States Army Air Corps became the United States Air Force on what date?
explanation: The U.S. Army Air Corps was officially reorganized into the independent United States Air Force on September 18, 1947.

title: The "Trail of Tears" was a result of which United States President's Indian Removal Policy?
wrong_answers: {"Harry S. Truman","Martin Van Buren","John Quincy Adams"}
explanation: President Andrew Jackson's Indian Removal Act of 1830 forced the relocation of southeastern tribes, most notably the Trail of Tears for the Cherokee in 1838-1839.

title: When did the Battle of the Somme begin?
explanation: The Battle of the Somme began on July 1, 1916, and lasted 141 days, becoming one of World War I's bloodiest battles with over 1 million casualties.

title: From 1940 to 1942, what was the capital-in-exile of Free France ?
explanation: Brazzaville, capital of French Equatorial Africa in Congo, served as Free France's capital-in-exile under General de Gaulle from 1940 to 1944.

title: Which of the following countries was not an axis power during World War II?
explanation: The Soviet Union was not an Axis power; it was invaded by Axis powers and fought alongside the Allies after June 1941.

title: Which of the following Assyrian kings did NOT rule during the Neo-Assyrian Empire?
explanation: Shamshi-Adad III ruled during the Old Assyrian period (1813-1791 BCE), centuries before the Neo-Assyrian Empire (911-609 BCE).

title: Who led the Communist Revolution of Russia?
explanation: Lenin led the October Revolution in 1917 and established the Soviet state as its founding leader.

title: Which of these landmarks is not included in the original 'Seven Wonders of the Ancient World'?
wrong_answers: {"Great Pyramid of Giza","Colossus of Rhodes","Hanging Gardens of Babylon"}
explanation: The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries, primarily in medieval times; the original Seven Wonders list was compiled by Hellenistic writers around the 2nd century BCE.

title: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States of America?
explanation: France gifted the Statue of Liberty to commemorate American independence and the alliance between the two nations.

title: Which of the following ancient Near Eastern peoples still exists as a modern ethnic group?
explanation: Assyrians, descendants of the ancient Assyrian Empire, persist as a distinct ethnic and religious minority in Iraq, Syria, and diaspora communities.

title: In what year did Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin land on the moon?
explanation: Apollo 11 landed on July 20–21, 1969, with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the lunar surface.

title: Who was the first man to travel into outer space twice?
explanation: Gus Grissom flew Mercury-Redstone 3 in 1961 and Gemini 3 in 1965, making him the first to travel into space twice.

title: Which king was killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485?
explanation: Richard III fell at Bosworth Field in 1485, ending the Plantagenet dynasty and establishing Tudor rule.

title: Who discovered Penicillin?
explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin accidentally in 1928 when mold contaminated his bacterial culture plates.

title: In what year was the last natural case of smallpox documented?
explanation: The last naturally occurring smallpox case was reported in Somalia in 1977; the disease was declared eradicated in 1980.

title: When did construction of the Suez Canal finish?
explanation: The Suez Canal opened to traffic on November 17, 1869, linking Europe and Asia via the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

title: In 1720, England was in massive debt and became involved in the South Sea Bubble. Who was the main mastermind behind it?
explanation: John Blunt was the master architect of the South Sea Company scheme, orchestrating the fraudulent investment bubble.

title: What Russian automatic gas-operated assault rifle was developed in the Soviet Union in 1947, and is still popularly used today?
explanation: Mikhail Kalashnikov designed the AK-47 in 1947; it became the world's most widely distributed assault rifle.

title: In addition to his career as an astrologer and "prophet", Nostradamus published a 1555 treatise that included a section on what?
wrong_answers: {"Teaching parrots to talk","Cheating at card games","Digging graves"}
explanation: Nostradamus published 'Traité des fardemens' in 1555, which included recipes for cosmetics, jams, and medicinal preparations.

title: What was the unofficial name for Germany between 1919 and 1933?
explanation: The Weimar Republic (1919–1933) was the official name of Germany's government between WWI and the Nazi takeover.

title: Who was the first President of the People's Republic of China?
explanation: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China on October 1, 1949, becoming its first president.

title: The ontological argument for the proof of God's existence is first attributed to whom?
explanation: Anselm of Canterbury (1033–1109) first formulated the ontological argument, defining God as the greatest conceivable being.

title: Which of these positions did the astronomer and physicist Isaac Newton not hold?
correct_answer: Surveyor to the City of London
wrong_answers: {"Professor of Mathematics","Warden of the Royal Mint","Member of Parliament"}
explanation: Newton held professor of mathematics, warden of the Royal Mint, and Parliament positions, but never surveyor to London.

title: The first Legoland park was opened in 1968 in which of these cities?
explanation: The original Legoland opened in Billund, Denmark in 1968, built around the Lego company's hometown and manufacturing base.

title: On what day did Germany invade Poland?
explanation: Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, triggering British and French declarations of war on September 3.

title: In what year was the video game company Electronic Arts founded?
explanation: Electronic Arts (EA) was founded on May 28, 1982, by Trip Hawkins and others as a publisher of computer games.

title: Which famous world leader is famed for the saying, "Let them eat cake", yet is rumored that he/she never said it at all?
explanation: The phrase 'Let them eat cake' is a myth likely invented by anti-royalist writers; no historical evidence links it to Marie Antoinette.

title: Which King of England was faced with the Peasants' Revolt in 1381?
explanation: Richard II faced the Peasants' Revolt in 1381, a major uprising triggered by poll taxes and feudal grievances.

title: When did the British hand-over sovereignty of Hong Kong back to China?
explanation: Hong Kong was handed back to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, 1997, under the 'one country, two systems' arrangement.

title: Who is attributed credit for recording the epic poem The Odyssey?
explanation: Homer is credited as the author of the Odyssey, an epic poem composed in the 8th century BCE (though authorship remains debated).

title: Who was the first ruler of Haiti after the country had gained its independence?
explanation: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared Haiti's independence on January 1, 1804, and served as its first leader.

title: Who was the first president of the United States?
explanation: George Washington was unanimously elected the first US president in 1788 and served two terms (1789–1797).

title: Which Irish village in County Mayo built a tourism industry on the back of an alleged appearance by the Virgin Mary in 1879?
explanation: In 1879, alleged apparitions of the Virgin Mary at Knock, County Mayo, drew pilgrims and established it as a major Catholic shrine.

title: The original Roman alphabet lacked the following letters EXCEPT:
explanation: The Roman alphabet originally lacked W, J, and U; X was one of the earliest letters derived from Phoenician xi.

title: Which historical conflict killed the most people?
explanation: WWII resulted in 70–85 million deaths, the deadliest conflict in human history by total casualties.

title: Who was Hannibal?
explanation: Hannibal (247–181 BCE) was a Carthaginian military commander and statesman famous for his campaigns against Rome.

title: When was Napoleon Bonaparte crowned emperor of the French?
explanation: Napoleon was crowned Emperor of the French on December 2, 1804, at Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris.

title: When did Canada leave the confederation to become their own nation?
explanation: Canada achieved Dominion status on July 1, 1867, through Confederation, gaining self-governance while remaining part of the British Empire.

title: Which WWII tank ace is credited with having destroyed the most tanks?
explanation: Kurt Knispel, a Czech-German tank commander, is credited with 168 confirmed tank kills during WWII.

title: In what dialogue did Socrates defend himself to the court of Athens?
explanation: In 'The Apology,' Socrates defends himself against charges of impiety and corrupting youth before the Athenian court in 399 BCE.

title: List the following Iranic empires in chronological order:
wrong_answers: {"Median, Achaemenid, Sassanid, Parthian","Achaemenid, Median, Parthian, Sassanid","Achaemenid, Median, Sassanid, Parthian"}
explanation: The Median (728–550 BCE), Achaemenid (550–330 BCE), Parthian (247 BCE–224 CE), and Sassanid (224–651 CE) empires represent Iran's major successive dynasties.

title: During WWII, in 1945, the United States dropped atomic bombs on the two Japanese cities of Hiroshima and what other city?
explanation: The US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima (August 6) and Nagasaki (August 9), 1945, hastening Japan's surrender.

title: Who was the leader of Sweden in the Great Northern War?
explanation: Charles XII of Sweden led military campaigns from 1697 to 1718, though he was ultimately defeated by Peter the Great.

title: What is the bloodiest event in United States history, in terms of casualties?
explanation: The Battle of Antietam (September 17, 1862) resulted in ~23,000 casualties, making it the bloodiest single day in US military history.

title: What year did Skoal, a smokeless Tobacco company, release their first line of Pouches, known as "Skoal Bandits"?
explanation: Skoal introduced Skoal Bandits, their first moist snuff pouches, in 1983, making smokeless tobacco more convenient.

title: In the year 1900, what were the most popular first names given to boy and girl babies born in the United States?
wrong_answers: {"Joseph and Catherine","William and Elizabeth","George and Anne"}
explanation: In 1900, John and Mary were the most popular baby names in the United States based on birth records.

title: Which South American country fought Great Britain over the Falkland Islands in 1982?
explanation: Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands in April 1982; Britain retook them after a 10-week war.

title: When was Adolf Hitler appointed as Chancellor of Germany?
explanation: Hitler was appointed Chancellor of Germany on January 30, 1933, beginning his consolidation of totalitarian power.

title: Which of these theoretical phycisists first predicted the existence of antimatter?
explanation: Paul Dirac predicted antimatter's existence in 1928 through his relativistic quantum mechanical equations.

title: In which year did the Tokyo Subway Sarin Attack occur?
explanation: The Tokyo Subway Sarin Attack occurred on March 20, 1995, by the Aum Shinrikyo cult, killing 13 people.

title: Which dictator killed the most people?
explanation: Mao Zedong's policies (Great Leap Forward, Cultural Revolution) are estimated to have caused 40–80 million deaths.

title: Which country were potatoes originally grown?
explanation: Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes Mountains of Peru around 7,000–10,000 years ago.

title: Which Las Vegas casino was originally constructed and operated by mobster Bugsy Siegel?
explanation: Bugsy Siegel built and opened the Flamingo casino in Las Vegas in 1946, pioneering modern luxury resort development.

title: What nationality was sultan Saladin?
explanation: Saladin (1137–1193) was born near Tikrit in modern-day Iraq to Kurdish parents, making him ethnically Kurdish.

title: The Little Entente was an alliance formed against which nation?
explanation: The Little Entente (1920–1938) was formed by Czechoslovakia, Romania, and Yugoslavia to counter Hungarian expansion.

title: The Panama Canal was finished under the administration of which U.S. president?
explanation: The Panama Canal was completed in August 1914; Woodrow Wilson was president and oversaw its opening to traffic.

title: On which day did the attempted coup d'etat of 1991 in the Soviet Union begin?
explanation: The 1991 Soviet coup attempt began on August 19 when hardliners sought to depose Mikhail Gorbachev.

title: What was the name of the first permanent English settlement in America?
explanation: Jamestown, Virginia (1607) was the first permanent English settlement in North America.

title: After the 1516 Battle of Marj Dabiq, the Ottoman Empire took control of Jerusalem from which sultanate?
explanation: After the 1516 Battle of Marj Dabiq, the Ottoman Empire conquered Jerusalem from the Mamluk Sultanate.

title: Which naval battle was considered the turning point of the Pacific Ocean Theater during World War 2?
wrong_answers: {"Attack on Truk Island","Attack on Pearl Harbor","Battle of the Coral Sea"}
explanation: The Battle of Midway (June 3–7, 1942) reversed Japanese naval dominance and marked the turning point in the Pacific War.

title: Which modern country is known as "The Graveyard of Empires"?
explanation: Afghanistan's rugged terrain, independent tribes, and fierce resistance have historically defeated multiple empires from Alexander to the Soviets.

title: In what year did the Great Northern War, between Russia and Sweden, end?
explanation: The Great Northern War between Russia and Sweden ended with the Treaty of Nystad on September 10, 1721.

title: What was the name commonly given to the ancient trade routes that connected the East and West of Eurasia?
explanation: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes connecting China, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe from ~2nd century BCE.

title: Which famous military commander marched an army, which included war elephants, over the Alps during the Second Punic War?
explanation: Hannibal crossed the Alps with war elephants and an army in 218 BCE during the Second Punic War against Rome.

title: The Arab Spring was a series of protests and rebellions that began in which of these Arab nations?
explanation: The Arab Spring began with self-immolation and protests in Tunisia on December 17, 2010, then spread across the Arab world.

title: When did Jamaica receive its independence from England?
explanation: Jamaica gained independence from the United Kingdom on August 6, 1962.

title: Which country did the Eureka Rebellion, an 1856 battle against colonial rule, take place in?
explanation: The Eureka Rebellion occurred in Victoria, Australia in 1854, a protest against unjust mining taxes and colonial authoritarianism.

title: In what year was the M1911 pistol designed?
explanation: The M1911 pistol was designed and adopted by the US military in 1911 as the standard-issue sidearm.

title: When was the SS or Schutzstaffel established?
explanation: The SS (Schutzstaffel) was established on April 4, 1925, as Hitler's paramilitary organization.

title: What did Albert Einstein win the Nobel Prize for in 1921?
explanation: Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

title: In what year did the nuclear power plant in Chernobyl melt down?
explanation: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred on April 26, 1986, in Soviet Ukraine, the worst nuclear accident in history.

title: During the Roman Triumvirate of 42 BCE, what region of the Roman Republic was given to Lepidus?
explanation: In the Second Triumvirate (42 BCE), Mark Antony, Octavian, and Lepidus divided power; Lepidus received Hispania (Spain and Portugal).

title: When did the French Revolution begin?
explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on July 14.

title: What is the name given to the series of confrontations between the UK and Iceland over North Atlantic fishing rights?
wrong_answers: {"The Lobster Wars","The Halibut Wars","The Mackerel Wars"}
explanation: The Cod Wars (1958–1961, 1972–1973, 1975–1976) were three confrontations between the UK and Iceland over North Atlantic fishing rights.

title: How many Sister Ships were related to the TItanic?
explanation: The Titanic had two sister ships: the RMS Olympic and HMHS Britannic (originally the HMSS Britannic).

title: According to legend, the ancient Greeks constructed a huge wooden model of which animal to gain entrance to Troy?
explanation: According to Greek legend, the Trojan Horse was a giant wooden horse used to smuggle Greek soldiers into Troy.

title: What was the bloodiest single-day battle during the American Civil War?
wrong_answers: {"The Siege of Vicksburg","The Battle of Gettysburg","The Battles of Chancellorsville"}
explanation: The Battle of Antietam on September 17, 1862, resulted in ~23,000 casualties, the bloodiest single day of the Civil War.

title: Who was the first man to travel into outer space?
explanation: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961, aboard Vostok 1.

title: The RMS Titanic sunk during her maiden voyage from Southampton, England to which American city?
explanation: The Titanic sank during its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City on April 15, 1912.

title: When did Vesuvius destroy the city of Pompeii?
explanation: Mount Vesuvius erupted on August 24, 79 AD, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice.

title: What was the name of the German offensive operation in October 1941 to take Moscow before winter?
explanation: Operation Typhoon (September–December 1941) was Nazi Germany's failed offensive to capture Moscow before winter.

title: Which U.S. President was famously 'attacked' by a swimming rabbit?
explanation: Jimmy Carter was attacked by a swimming rabbit near his boat in 1979, an incident memorialized in White House records.

title: What was Genghis Khan's real name?
explanation: Genghis Khan's birth name was Temüjin; he took the title Genghis Khan ('universal ruler') after unifying the Mongol tribes.

title: How old was the famous King Tutankhamen (Tut) when he died?
explanation: King Tutankhamen died at age 19 around 1323 BCE; modern analysis suggests complications from a leg fracture and malaria.

title: The collapse of the Soviet Union took place in which year?
explanation: The Soviet Union officially dissolved on December 26, 1991, ending the Cold War.

title: In what year was the famous 45 foot tall Hollywood sign first erected?
explanation: The Hollywood sign was erected in 1923 on Mount Lee in the Hollywood Hills, originally an advertisement for a local real estate development.

title: What event marked the start of World War II?
wrong_answers: {"Invasion of Russia (1942)","Battle of Britain (1940)","Invasion of Normandy (1944)"}
explanation: Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, marked the start of World War II in Europe.

title: In what year did Texas secede from Mexico?
explanation: Texas declared independence from Mexico on March 2, 1836, establishing the Republic of Texas until annexation in 1845.

title: Which Nazi General was known as the "Desert Fox"?
explanation: Erwin Rommel earned the 'Desert Fox' nickname commanding the Afrika Korps in North Africa during WWII.

title: The catastrophic nuclear accident that occurred in Ukraine in 1986 occurred at which power plant?
explanation: The Chernobyl Nuclear Power Station in Ukraine experienced a catastrophic meltdown on April 26, 1986.

title: Which of these founding fathers of the United States of America later became president?
explanation: James Monroe, a signer of the Declaration of Independence and diplomat, served as the fifth US president (1817–1825).

title: What year did the Vietnam War end?
explanation: The Vietnam War ended on April 30, 1975, with North Vietnam's capture of Saigon and the fall of South Vietnam.

title: What was William Frederick Cody better known as?
explanation: William Frederick Cody was better known as Buffalo Bill, a showman and Wild West figure of the late 19th century.

title: In what year did William the Conqueror take control of England?
explanation: William the Conqueror defeated English King Harold at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, establishing Norman rule.

title: Which of the following physicists did NOT work on the Manhattan project?
explanation: Murray Gell-Mann developed the quark model in the 1960s; he did not work on the Manhattan Project.

title: Who was the first mammal successfully launched into Earth's orbit?
wrong_answers: {"Ham, the chimpanzee","Baker, the monkey","Belka, the dog"}
explanation: Laika, a Soviet dog, became the first mammal in orbit aboard Sputnik 2 on November 3, 1957.

title: Which one of these countries was NOT in the Central Powers during WWI?
explanation: Spain remained neutral during WWI, not joining the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire).

title: What was Manfred von Richthofen's nickname?
wrong_answers: {"The High Flying Ace","The Blue Serpent","The Germany Gunner"}
explanation: Manfred von Richthofen, a German fighter pilot with 80 confirmed kills, was known as the Red Baron.

title: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, symbolizing the collapse of communist East Germany and the Cold War's end.

title: In 1547 who became the 1st Tsar of Russia
explanation: Ivan IV (Ivan the Terrible) became the first Tsar of Russia in 1547, consolidating power and expanding the Moscow state.

title: On what street did the 1666 Great Fire of London start?
explanation: The Great Fire of London in 1666 started on Pudding Lane in a bakery owned by Thomas Farriner.

title: Which of the following snipers has the highest amount of confirmed kills?
explanation: Simo Häyhä, a Finnish sniper, had 505–542 confirmed kills during the Winter War (1939–1940).

title: Which of these countries was NOT a part of the Soviet Union?
explanation: Afghanistan was never formally part of the Soviet Union; it was occupied by Soviet forces (1979–1989) but remained independent.

title: Who tutored Alexander the Great?
explanation: Aristotle tutored Alexander the Great from 343 to 340 BCE, profoundly influencing his worldview and ambitions.

title: How was Socrates executed?
explanation: Socrates was sentenced to death by Athenian court in 399 BCE for corrupting youth and impiety; he drank hemlock poison as the method of execution.

title: Who was the first president of Kenya?
explanation: Jomo Kenyatta led Kenya to independence from Britain in 1964 and served as the country's first president until his death in 1978.

title: Who crowned Charlemagne as Holy Roman Emperor on Christmas Day in 800?
explanation: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne on Christmas Day 800 at Saint Peter's Basilica, establishing the Holy Roman Empire and legitimizing his rule over Western Europe.

title: What micro-state is considered to have the oldest constitution still in effect?
explanation: San Marino's constitution, dated 1600, is the oldest surviving national constitution still in continuous effect, predating others by centuries.

title: Toussaint Louverture led a successful slave revolt in which country?
explanation: Toussaint Louverture led a successful slave rebellion in Haiti (then Saint-Domingue) from 1791-1804, resulting in the first independent Black republic.

title: Where was Napoleon Bonaparte born?
explanation: Napoleon Bonaparte was born on August 15, 1769, in Ajaccio on the island of Corsica, which had just become part of France.

title: Which English king was married to Eleanor of Aquitaine?
explanation: Henry II of England married Eleanor of Aquitaine in 1152, uniting their vast territorial holdings and becoming one of medieval Europe's most powerful couples.

title: During the Spanish Civil War (1936), Francisco Franco fought for which political faction?
explanation: Franco led the Nationalist faction during Spain's Civil War, supported by fascist powers Germany and Italy, defeating the Republican government by 1939.

title: What was found in 1946 by two young shepards near a cave?
wrong_answers: {"The Blackbeard Chest","Sheep","The First Oaxaca Cave Sleeper"}
explanation: Two Bedouin shepherds discovered the Dead Sea Scrolls near Qumran in 1946, ancient Hebrew texts containing biblical books and religious documents dated around 2000 years old.

title: Spain was formed in 1469 with the marriage of Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of what other Iberian kingdom?
explanation: The marriage of Isabella I and Ferdinand II of Aragon in 1469 unified the two kingdoms and laid the foundation for the modern Spanish state.

title: When was the People's Republic of China founded?
explanation: The People's Republic of China was founded on October 1, 1949, following Mao Zedong's victory in the Chinese Civil War and Communist takeover of the mainland.

title: In 1961, an American B-52 aircraft crashed and nearly detonated two 4mt nuclear bombs over which US city?
explanation: A B-52 crashed near Goldsboro, North Carolina, on January 24, 1961, carrying two thermonuclear bombs that nearly detonated in what has been called the closest call to accidental nuclear war.

title: One of the deadliest pandemics, the "Spanish Flu", killed off what percentage of the human world population at the time?
wrong_answers: {"6 to 10 percent","1 to 3 percent","less than 1 percent"}
explanation: The 1918-1920 Spanish Flu pandemic killed an estimated 3-6% of the world's 1.8 billion population, making it one of history's deadliest pandemics.

title: What was the code name for the Allied invasion of Southern France on August 15th, 1944?
explanation: Operation Dragoon was the August 1944 Allied invasion of southern France, designed to secure Mediterranean ports and support the Normandy campaign.

title: Which one of these rulers did not belong to the Habsburg dynasty?
explanation: Philip V was the first Bourbon king of Spain (r. 1700-1746), breaking the Habsburg dynasty's 200-year rule over the Spanish throne.

title: In 1845, a series of wars named after which indigenous people began in New Zealand?
explanation: The Māori Wars (1845-1872) began in 1845 and represent a series of conflicts between British colonial forces and indigenous Māori peoples in New Zealand.

title: Abolitionist John Brown raided the arsenal in which Virginia Town?
explanation: John Brown raided the Federal Arsenal at Harpers Ferry, Virginia, on October 16, 1859, attempting to incite a slave rebellion that was quickly suppressed.

title: When was Google founded?
explanation: Google was founded on September 4, 1998, by Larry Page and Sergey Brin as a search engine project born from their Stanford University research.

title: In the Seven Wonders of the World, which wonder is the only that has survived to this day?
wrong_answers: {"Colossus of Rhodes","Lighthouse of Alexandria","Statue of Zeus at Olympia"}
explanation: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the sole surviving wonder of the ancient Seven Wonders of the World, having stood for over 4,600 years despite earthquakes and erosion.

title: In what year did the Battle of Verdun take place?
explanation: The Battle of Verdun, one of WWI's bloodiest battles, lasted from February 21 to December 18, 1916, resulting in roughly 700,000 combined casualties.

title: The Spitfire L.F. Mk IX had what engine?
explanation: The Spitfire L.F. Mk IX, a late-war variant optimized for low-altitude combat, was powered by the Merlin 66 engine producing enhanced supercharger performance.

title: Hong Kong was a part of which country's territory before Britain regained it in 1945?
explanation: Hong Kong was occupied by Japan from 1941-1945 during WWII before Britain retook control after Japan's surrender in August 1945.

title: The minigun was designed in 1960 by which manufacturer.
explanation: General Electric designed the minigun in 1960 under engineer Robert Woodhead's leadership, creating a rapid-fire weapon system that became a military standard.

title: When is the Ides of March?
explanation: The Ides of March in the Roman calendar fall on March 15; the date is infamous as the day Julius Caesar was assassinated in 44 BCE.

title: Who is the creator of the soft drink, Dr. Pepper?
explanation: Charles Alderton, a pharmacist at Morrison's Old Corner Drug Store in Waco, Texas, invented Dr Pepper in 1885 as a proprietary soft drink formula.

title: Which of the following years is commonly referred to as the "Year Without a Summer"?
explanation: 1816 was the 'Year Without a Summer' caused by the eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia, which ejected vast ash clouds blocking sunlight worldwide.

title: What was the capital of South Vietnam before the Vietnam War?
explanation: Saigon was South Vietnam's capital until the country's fall to North Vietnam on April 30, 1975; it was renamed Ho Chi Minh City after reunification.

title: The gunpowder plot was a well-known failed assassination attempt against which of England's then reigning monarchs?
explanation: The Gunpowder Plot targeted King James I on November 5, 1605, when Guy Fawkes and fellow conspirators attempted to blow up Parliament and the royal family.

title: Under which name was Rodrigo Borgia made Pope?
explanation: Rodrigo Borgia became Pope Alexander VI in 1492, serving until 1503; he is remembered for nepotism, alleged corruption, and fathering several children while pope.

title: Which of the following battles is often considered as marking the beginning of the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
wrong_answers: {"Battle of Thessalonica","Battle of Pollentia","Battle of Constantinople"}
explanation: The Battle of Adrianople in 378 CE, where Roman legions were defeated by Visigothic cavalry, symbolized Rome's military decline and began the barbarian invasions.

title: What year did the Boxing Day earthquake & tsunami occur in the Indian Ocean?
explanation: The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami on December 26 killed over 230,000 people, making it one of history's deadliest natural disasters.

title: With which Greek philosopher would you associate the phrase, "I know that I know nothing"?
explanation: Socrates famously said 'I know that I know nothing' as an expression of philosophical humility and recognition of the limits of human knowledge.

title: Which game was the Game of the Year in 2018?
wrong_answers: {"Detroit: Become Human","Red Dead Redemption 2","A Way Out"}
explanation: God of War won Game of the Year 2018 from multiple award organizations, praised for its narrative depth, combat design, and character development.

title: What country joined the EU in 2013?
explanation: Croatia joined the European Union on July 1, 2013, becoming the first post-Yugoslav state and 28th EU member at that time.

title: The Bohemian Revolt (1618-1620) started after Protestants in Prague did what to their Catholic Lords Regents?
correct_answer: Threw them out of a window
wrong_answers: {"Insulted their mothers","Locked them in stockades","Hung them."}
explanation: During the Bohemian Revolt, Protestant nobles threw three Catholic regents out of Prague Castle's window (the Defenestration of Prague) on May 23, 1618.

title: The idea of Socialism was articulated and advanced by whom?
explanation: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels developed socialism as a political and economic theory, with Marx's works like The Communist Manifesto (1848) providing its philosophical foundation.

title: The crown of the Empire State Building was originally built for what purpose?
explanation: The Empire State Building's crown was originally designed with a mooring mast for zeppelins, though this purpose was never realized.

title: America's Strategic Defense System during the Cold War was nicknamed after this famous movie.
explanation: The Strategic Defense Initiative, announced by President Reagan in 1983, was nicknamed 'Star Wars' due to its futuristic space-based missile defense concept.

title: Who was the leader of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia ?
explanation: Josip Broz Tito led Yugoslavia's Communist Party and served as the country's president until 1980, holding the fractious federation together through his authority.

title: Which infamous European traitor was known as "the last person to enter Parliament with honest intentions"?
explanation: Guy Fawkes is remembered as 'the last person to enter Parliament with honest intentions' due to the failed Gunpowder Plot, a darkly ironic phrase.

title: Which of the following Presidents of the United States was assassinated?
explanation: William McKinley was assassinated by Leon Czolgosz on September 6, 1901, making him the third U.S. president to be killed in office.

title: Which one of these tanks was designed and operated by the United Kingdom?
explanation: The Tog II was a British experimental heavy tank designed during WWII, never seeing combat; it remains the heaviest tank ever built.

title: In which year did the Invasion of Kuwait by Iraq occur?
explanation: Iraq, under Saddam Hussein, invaded and annexed Kuwait on August 2, 1990, triggering the 1991 Gulf War and international military intervention.

title: During the Mongolian invasions of Japan, what were the Mongol boats mostly stopped by?
explanation: Two Mongol invasion fleets were destroyed by typhoons (kamikaze) in 1274 and 1281, preventing Kublai Khan's conquest of Japan.

title: When was the United States National Security Agency established?
explanation: The National Security Agency (NSA) was established on November 4, 1952, created to centralize signals intelligence operations during the early Cold War.

title: Which Australian Prime Minister disappeared in 1967 and was never found?
explanation: Australian Prime Minister Harold Holt disappeared on December 17, 1967, while swimming at Cheviot Beach; his body was never found, remaining one of history's great mysteries.

title: What was the official German currency until 2002?
explanation: The Deutsche Mark was Germany's official currency from 1948-2002; it was replaced by the Euro as part of European monetary unification.

title: The Ottoman Empire was dissolved after their loss in which war?
explanation: The Ottoman Empire collapsed after its defeat in World War I; the Treaty of Lausanne (1923) officially dissolved the 600-year-old empire.

title: Which of these countries remained neutral during World War II?
explanation: Switzerland maintained official neutrality throughout WWII despite German pressure, though it engaged in controversial banking and trade activities with the Axis.

title: What year did Australia become a federation?
explanation: Australia became a federation on January 1, 1901, uniting six separate British colonies into a single commonwealth nation.

title: Which Apollo mission was the last one in NASA's Apollo program?
explanation: Apollo 17 was the final Apollo mission in December 1972, marking the last time humans walked on the Moon until future Artemis missions.

title: Who was the first explorer to sail to North America?
explanation: Leif Erikson, a Norse explorer and son of Erik the Red, reached North America around 1000 CE, nearly 500 years before Columbus.

title: Which of his six wives was Henry VIII married to the longest?
explanation: Henry VIII was married to Catherine of Aragon for 24 years (1509-1533), longer than any of his other five marriages combined.

title: Who invented the "Flying Shuttle" in 1738; one of the key developments in the industrialization of weaving?
explanation: John Kay invented the flying shuttle in 1733 (not 1738), revolutionizing weaving by allowing faster cloth production on wider looms.

title: According to scholarly estimates, what percentage of the world population at the time died due to Tamerlane's conquests?
explanation: Timur's (Tamerlane's) conquests from 1369-1405 killed an estimated 5% of the world's population, making him one of history's deadliest conquerors.

title: These two countries held a commonwealth from the 16th to 18th century.
wrong_answers: {"Hutu and Rwanda","North Korea and South Korea","Bangladesh and Bhutan"}
explanation: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (1569-1795) was a powerful federation of two nations that made them a major European political and military force.

title: What were the first states to break away from Yugoslavia?
explanation: Slovenia and Croatia were the first two republics to declare independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, starting the Yugoslav Wars and the federation's dissolution.

title: What was the real name of the Albanian national leader Skanderbeg?
explanation: Skanderbeg was the Christian-born Albanian military commander whose real name was Gjergj Kastrioti; he fought Ottoman expansion for decades in the 15th century.

title: What year did World War II end?
explanation: World War II ended in 1945: Germany surrendered on May 7-8 (VE Day), and Japan surrendered on August 14-15 (VJ Day) after atomic bombings.

title: Which of these facilities was not present on the Titanic?
explanation: The Titanic featured a Turkish bath, heated swimming pool, kennel for passengers' pets, and a squash court, but no 'fainting room' as a named facility.

title: On which aircraft carrier did the Doolitte Raid launch from on April 18, 1942 during World War II?
explanation: The Doolittle Raid launched from the USS Hornet on April 18, 1942, sending B-25 bombers to raid Tokyo in a symbolic strike against Japan.

title: In what year did Kentucky become the 15th state to join the union?
explanation: Kentucky entered the Union on June 1, 1792, becoming the 15th state and the first state admitted after the original thirteen.

title: Who was the first president born in the independent United States?
explanation: Martin Van Buren, elected president in 1836, was the first president born as a U.S. citizen; all previous presidents were born before American independence.

title: Where was Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan killed in 1521?
explanation: Ferdinand Magellan was killed on April 27, 1521, at the Battle of Mactan in the Philippines while fighting indigenous warriors resisting colonization.

title: In 1453, which important city fell?
explanation: Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks on May 29, 1453, ending the thousand-year Byzantine Empire and reshaping Mediterranean geopolitics forever.

title: What was the original name of New York City?
explanation: New Amsterdam was the Dutch colony's name for New York (1624-1664) before the English took control and renamed it New York.

title: Adolf Hitler was born on which date?
explanation: Adolf Hitler was born on April 20, 1889, in Linz, Austria-Hungary, near the border with Bavaria.

title: Where and when was the first cardboard box made for industrial use?
explanation: The first industrial cardboard box was manufactured in England in 1817, marking the beginning of mass-produced packaging.

title: When did Spanish Peninsular War start?
explanation: The Peninsular War began in 1808 when Napoleon invaded Spain, triggering a prolonged conflict that lasted until 1814.

title: What was the Canada's first capital?
explanation: Kingston, Ontario, served as Canada's first capital from 1841-1844 before the capital moved to Montreal, then Ottawa.

title: When was the Gregorian Calendar first adopted?
explanation: Pope Gregory XIII introduced the Gregorian Calendar in 1582 to correct the Julian Calendar's drift, which has been gradually adopted worldwide.

title: In relation to the British Occupation in Ireland, what does the IRA stand for.
explanation: The Irish Republican Army (IRA) was formed in 1919 as a militant organization seeking Irish independence from British rule.

title: Which building was set aflame on August 24th, 1812?
wrong_answers: {"Parliament Building","Grand National Assembly Building","Palace of the Nation"}
explanation: The White House was burned by British forces on August 24, 1814, during the War of 1812 as retaliation for American attacks on Canada.

title: The main objective of the German operation "Case Blue" during World War II was originally to capture what?
explanation: Operation Blue (Fall Blau) in 1942 aimed to capture the oil fields of the Caucasus, though it became bogged down in the Stalingrad campaign.

title: Where did first known lesbian rights organization in the United States, Daughters of Bilitis, start?
explanation: The Daughters of Bilitis, founded in 1955 in San Francisco, was the first known lesbian rights organization in the United States.

title: How many years did the Hundred Years' War last?
explanation: The Hundred Years' War actually lasted 116 years (1337-1453), not 100, spanning English and French dynastic conflicts over the French throne.

title: Which day did World War I begin?
explanation: World War I officially began on July 28, 1914, when Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

title: The Battle of Hastings was fought in which year?
explanation: The Battle of Hastings on October 14, 1066, resulted in Norman victory and established William the Conqueror's rule over England, reshaping European history.

title: Which countries participated in the Lobster War?
wrong_answers: {"Canada and Norway","Australia and New Zealand","United States and England"}
explanation: The Lobster War (1961-1963) between France and Brazil was a diplomatic dispute over fishing rights off Brazil's coast, fought without military violence.

title: What year is considered to be the year that the British Empire ended?
explanation: 1997 marks the end of the British Empire, symbolized by the handover of Hong Kong to China on July 1, 1997, Britain's last major colonial territory.

title: The Fallingwater House, located in Pennsylvania, was designed by which architect?
explanation: Frank Lloyd Wright designed Fallingwater in 1935, an architectural masterpiece built over a waterfall in Pennsylvania exemplifying organic architecture.

title: Who was the only US President to be elected four times?
explanation: Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected president four times (1932, 1936, 1940, 1944), serving until his death in 1945; his reelection led to the two-term limit.

title: What battle was the longest in World War I, lasting approximately 303 days?
wrong_answers: {"Battle of Passchendaele","Battle of Amiens","Battle of Stalingrad"}
explanation: The Battle of Verdun lasted 303 days (Feb-Dec 1916), becoming WWI's longest and costliest battle with over 700,000 combined casualties.

title: Which is the hull NO. of the Fletcher class destroyer Fletcher?
explanation: USS Fletcher (DD-445) was the lead ship of the Fletcher-class destroyer, one of the most important destroyer classes in U.S. naval history.

title: Which country was an allied power in World War II?
explanation: The Soviet Union was an Allied power in WWII, joining after Nazi Germany's 1941 invasion and fighting until Japan's surrender in 1945.

title: What year was the United States Declaration of Independence signed?
explanation: The Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776, in Philadelphia, formally declaring the thirteen colonies' separation from British rule.

title: In which year was Nelson Mandela released from prison
explanation: Nelson Mandela was released from Victor Verster Prison on February 11, 1990, after 27 years of imprisonment, marking a turning point in South Africa's transition.

title: What was the name of the African-American cultural explosion centered in upper Manhattan during the 1920s and 1930s?
explanation: The Harlem Renaissance (1920s-1930s) was a cultural flowering of African-American art, literature, music, and intellectual achievement centered in Harlem, New York.

title: On which day did construction start on "The Pentagon", the headquarters for the United States Department of Defense?
explanation: Construction on the Pentagon began on September 11, 1941, in Arlington, Virginia, and the building was completed in just 16 months.

title: To what political party did Abraham Lincoln belong when elected POTUS?
explanation: Abraham Lincoln was elected as a Republican in 1860, the party's first successful presidential candidate, and served until his assassination in 1865.

title: When Christopher Columbus sailed to America, what was the first region he arrived in?
explanation: Columbus's first landfall in the Americas on October 12, 1492, was the Bahamas Archipelago (likely San Salvador), not mainland North America.

title: Who was the last emperor of Mexico?
wrong_answers: {"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","Napoleon III","Agustín de Iturbide"}
explanation: Ferdinand Maximilian was executed on June 19, 1867, ending the French-backed Second Mexican Empire and his brief reign as emperor.

title: How long did World War II last?
explanation: World War II lasted approximately 6 years, from Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, to Japan's surrender on September 2, 1945.

title: In which year did the First World War begin?
explanation: World War I began in 1914 when Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on July 28, following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

title: During what war did the "Cuban Missile Crisis" occur?
explanation: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962) occurred during the Cold War when the Soviet Union placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, bringing superpowers to the brink.

title: When was Finland's 100th year of being independent?
explanation: Finland celebrated 100 years of independence in 2017, having declared independence from Russia on December 6, 1917.

title: What happened on June 6, 1944?
wrong_answers: {"Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki","Attack on Pearl Harbor","The Liberation of Paris"}
explanation: D-Day on June 6, 1944, was the Normandy invasion launching the Western Allies' major offensive to liberate Nazi-occupied Western Europe.

title: Who was the first wife of King Henry VIII?
explanation: Catherine of Aragon was Henry VIII's first wife, married from 1509-1533; her inability to bear a son led to the English Reformation.

title: The son of which pope supposedly held a lecherous fête involving 50 courtesans in the papal palace?
explanation: Pope Alexander VI's son Cesare Borgia allegedly hosted a lavish banquet involving 50 courtesans at the papal palace, scandalizing Renaissance Rome.

title: Which of these countries was sea charted in 1500 by the Portuguese maritime explorations?
explanation: Pedro Álvares Cabral led a Portuguese fleet that reached Brazil in April 1500, establishing the first documented European contact with South America's eastern coast.

title: During World War I, which nation's monarchs were blood related?
wrong_answers: {"France, Russia, Germany","Serbia, Russia, Croatia","Germany, Spain, Austria"}
explanation: King George V of Britain, Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany, and Tsar Nicholas II of Russia were all grandchildren of Queen Victoria, making them first cousins united by blood.

title: When did Lithuania declare independence from the Soviet Union?
explanation: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, establishing itself as a sovereign state before the USSR's official dissolution in December 1991.

title: What was the transfer of disease, crops, and people across the Atlantic shortly after the discovery of the Americas called?
explanation: The Columbian Exchange refers to the massive transfer of plants, animals, diseases, and people between the Old and New Worlds following Columbus's 1492 voyage, reshaping both hemispheres.

title: The Korean War started in what year?
explanation: North Korea invaded South Korea on June 25, 1950, marking the beginning of the Korean War, which lasted until 1953 with an armistice agreement.

title: Who was a military strategist in the Eastern Zhou period?
explanation: Sun Tzu (c. 544-496 BCE) was a legendary Chinese military strategist during the Eastern Zhou period, renowned for authoring the classical text 'The Art of War'.

title: Pianist Frédéric Chopin was a composer of which musical era?
explanation: Frédéric Chopin (1810-1849) was a defining figure of the Romantic era, composing expressive, emotionally complex works that epitomized the period's musical values.

title: What year did World War I begin?
explanation: World War I began on July 28, 1914, when Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, escalating into a continental conflict.

title: During the Wars of the Roses (1455 - 1487) which Englishman was dubbed "the Kingmaker"?
explanation: Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick, earned the title 'Kingmaker' for his pivotal role in placing and deposing English monarchs during the Wars of the Roses.

title: When did O, Canada officially become the national anthem?
explanation: 'O, Canada' officially became Canada's national anthem in 1980, replacing 'God Save the Queen' as the official symbol of Canadian identity.

title: The Hagia Sophia was commissioned by which emperor of the Byzantine Empire?
explanation: Emperor Justinian I commissioned the Hagia Sophia in 532 CE, constructing it as a patriarchal cathedral and one of the most architecturally revolutionary buildings of its time.

title: King Henry VIII was the second monarch of which European royal house?
explanation: Henry VIII was the second Tudor monarch, following his father Henry VII who founded the Tudor dynasty in 1485 after defeating Richard III at Bosworth Field.

title: Which U.S. President was in office when the Gulf War began?
explanation: George H. W. Bush was president when Iraq invaded Kuwait on August 2, 1990, triggering Operation Desert Storm, which commenced in January 1991.

title: Which of the following was Brazil was a former colony under?
explanation: Portugal colonized Brazil in 1500 when Pedro Álvares Cabral arrived, establishing Portuguese dominance that lasted until Brazilian independence in 1822.

title: What is the historical name of Sri Lanka?
explanation: Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon during British colonial rule (1796-1948), taking its current name upon independence in recognition of its indigenous heritage.

title: Which modern day country is the region that was known as Phrygia in ancient times?
explanation: Phrygia was an ancient kingdom in west-central Anatolia, now part of modern-day Turkey, known historically for the Phrygian language and cultural influence.

title: The seed drill was invented by which British inventor?
explanation: Jethro Tull invented the seed drill in 1701, revolutionizing agriculture by allowing precise, efficient planting of seeds in rows rather than scattering them.

title: What year was the Italian firearms manufacturer Beretta founded?
explanation: Beretta, the Italian firearms manufacturer, was founded in 1526 in Brescia, making it one of the oldest continuously operating manufacturing companies in the world.

title: Which of the following countries was the first to send an object into space?
explanation: Germany launched V-2 rockets into space as early as 1944; the captured German V-2 was adapted postwar and became the basis for U.S. and Soviet space programs.

title: Who rode on horseback to warn the Minutemen that the British were coming during the U.S. Revolutionary War?
explanation: Paul Revere's midnight ride on April 18, 1775, alerted Massachusetts colonists to the British military movement, enabling militia to assemble before the Battles of Lexington and Concord.

title: Pol Pot was the former dictator of which country?
explanation: Pol Pot led the Khmer Rouge and served as dictator of Cambodia (1975-1979), presiding over the Cambodian genocide that killed approximately 1.7-2 million people.

title: Who is believed to have been the first European to 'discover' the land of New Zealand?
explanation: Abel Tasman, a Dutch explorer, reached New Zealand in 1642, making him the first known European to sail to the islands, though he did not land.

title: What disease crippled President Franklin D. Roosevelt and led him to help the nation find a cure?
explanation: Franklin D. Roosevelt contracted poliomyelitis in 1921 at age 39, becoming paralyzed; his personal struggle with the disease motivated his support for medical research.

title: Which U.S. president took part in the Potsdam Conference, where the Allies reached a peace settlement with Germany?
explanation: Harry S. Truman attended the Potsdam Conference in July-August 1945 as president, replacing Franklin D. Roosevelt after his death in April.

title: Who was the British Prime Minister at the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939?
explanation: Neville Chamberlain was Prime Minister when Nazi Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, though Winston Churchill succeeded him on May 10, 1940.

title: What was the last colony the UK ceded marking the end of the British Empire?
explanation: Hong Kong was the last significant British colony, handed over to China on July 1, 1997, symbolizing the end of the British Empire's territorial dominion.

title: What does the United States of America celebrate during the 4th of July?
correct_answer: The signing of the Declaration of Independence
wrong_answers: {"The anniversary of the Battle of Gettysburg","The crossing of the Delaware River","The ratification of the Constitution"}
explanation: July 4 commemorates the Declaration of Independence signed on July 4, 1776, formally announcing the thirteen colonies' separation from British rule.

title: Who succeded Josef Stalin as the leader of the Soviet Union?
explanation: Nikita Khrushchev became Soviet leader after Stalin's death in 1953, eventually gaining supreme power by the late 1950s and implementing de-Stalinization reforms.

title: Which of these 1900s tanks were designed and built BEFORE the others?
explanation: The Renault FT (1917) was the world's first tank with a fully rotating turret, preceding the M4 Sherman (1942), Panzer IV (1936), and Cromwell (1943) tanks.

title: How many sonatas did Ludwig van Beethoven write?
explanation: Ludwig van Beethoven composed 32 piano sonatas throughout his life, from his early works through his revolutionary late period compositions.

title: What is widely considered to be the oldest civilization known to mankind?
explanation: Sumer (c. 3500 BCE) is considered the oldest known civilization, featuring the first writing system (cuneiform), cities, and complex social structures.

title: Which Louis was known as 'The Sun King of France'?
explanation: Louis XIV of France (1638-1715) earned the epithet 'The Sun King' due to his absolute power, long reign, and cultural dominance during the height of French grandeur.

title: Which of the following Soviet revolutionaries was exiled from the USSR and later assassinated in 1940 for criticizing Stalinism?
explanation: Leon Trotsky, founder of the Red Army, was exiled by Stalin in 1929 for opposing Stalinism and was assassinated in Mexico on August 20, 1940, by a Soviet agent.

title: How old was Adolf Hitler when he died?
explanation: Adolf Hitler was born on April 20, 1889, and died on April 30, 1945, at age 56, committing suicide in his Berlin bunker as Soviet forces closed in.

title: What was the name of the national hero of the Philippines who inspired and lead the Philippine Revolution against colonial Spain?
explanation: José Rizal (1861-1896) was a Filipino nationalist writer and reformer whose works and advocacy inspired the Philippine Revolution against Spanish colonial rule.

title: What was the name of the planned invasion of Japan towards the end of World War II?
explanation: Operation Downfall was the planned 1945-1946 U.S. invasion of Japan, comprising Operation Olympic (assault on Kyushu) and Operation Coronet (assault on Honshu).

title: Which country was Josef Stalin born in?
explanation: Joseph Stalin was born in Gori, Georgia in 1878; he adopted his Russified name early in his revolutionary career despite his Georgian ethnicity and accent.

title: Which country attacked the USS Liberty on June 8, 1967?
explanation: Israel attacked the USS Liberty on June 8, 1967, killing 34 sailors and wounding 171 in an incident during the Six-Day War; Israel claimed it was a case of mistaken identity.

title: Which country had an "Orange Revolution" between 2004 and 2005?
explanation: Ukraine's Orange Revolution (2004-2005) protested fraudulent election results and resulted in the annulment of the disputed presidential election victory.

title: Who was the first prime minister of Canada?
explanation: John A. Macdonald served as Canada's first Prime Minister from 1867 to 1873 and again from 1878 to 1891, playing a central role in Confederation.

title: Joseph Stalin had a criminal past doing what?
explanation: Young Stalin was arrested multiple times and exiled to Siberia; he earned money by robbing trains and orchestrating criminal activities for Bolshevik funds.

title: What did the first vending machines in the early 1880's dispense?
explanation: Early 1880s vending machines dispensed postcards; users inserted a coin to receive a card, predating later machines that sold candy, cigarettes, or other goods.

title: The Thirty Years War ended with which treaty?
wrong_answers: {"Treaty of Versailles","Treaty of Paris","Peace of Prague"}
explanation: The Peace of Westphalia (1648) ended the Thirty Years' War in Europe, establishing principles of state sovereignty and religious tolerance that shaped modern international law.

title: In what year did the First World War end?
explanation: World War I ended on November 11, 1918, with the armistice agreement, officially ending combat operations and leading to the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.

title: When was "The Gadget", the first nuclear device to be detonated, tested?
explanation: The Trinity test of 'the Gadget' (first nuclear bomb) occurred on July 16, 1945, in New Mexico, opening the atomic age with a successful 22-kiloton detonation.

title: The assassination of which royal led to the start of World War I?
explanation: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria was assassinated on June 28, 1914, by Serbian nationalist Gavrilo Princip, triggering Austria-Hungary's declaration of war and World War I.

title: Which of the following African countries was most successful in resisting colonization?
explanation: Ethiopia successfully resisted Italian colonization, defeating the Italians at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, preserving independence and becoming a symbol of African resistance.

title: What did the abbreviation "RMS" stand for in the RMS Titanic in 1912?
wrong_answers: {"Royal Majesty Service","Regular Maritime Schedule","Regulated Maelstrom Sensor"}
explanation: RMS stands for 'Royal Mail Ship', designating vessels contracted to carry Royal Mail; the Titanic held a Royal Mail contract when it sank in 1912.

title: How many women joined the United States Armed Services during World War II?
explanation: Approximately 350,000 women served in the U.S. Armed Forces during World War II, contributing as nurses, pilots, code-breakers, and in other military and support roles.

title: Which of the following is NOT classified as a Semetic language?
explanation: Sumerian is not a Semitic language; it is a language isolate from ancient Mesopotamia, while Maltese, Akkadian, and Mandaic are all Semitic languages.

title: What day did the Battle of Gettysburg begin?
explanation: The Battle of Gettysburg commenced on July 1, 1863, in Pennsylvania, the turning point of the Civil War and the largest battle fought on North American soil.

title: Which U.S. president was said to have been too honest to lie to his father about chopping down a cherry tree?
explanation: The cherry tree anecdote about George Washington's honesty is a myth created by his biographer Mason Locke Weems and has no historical basis.

title: Which British monarch was also known as "William of Orange"?
explanation: William III (1650-1702) was also known as William of Orange, a Dutch prince who became King of England after the Glorious Revolution of 1688.

title: What was Napoleon Bonaparte's name before he changed it?
wrong_answers: {"Naapolion van Bonijpaart","Napoleão do Boaparte","Napoleona de Buenoparte"}
explanation: Napoleon Bonaparte's birth name was Napoleone Buonaparte; he Gallicized it to Napoleon Bonaparte after moving to mainland France as a young officer.

title: When did the Byzantine Empire collapse?
explanation: The Byzantine Empire fell on May 29, 1453, when Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople, ending over 1,000 years of Byzantine rule.

title: The Herero genocide was perpetrated in Africa by which of the following colonial nations?
explanation: The German Empire perpetrated the Herero genocide in German South-West Africa (1904-1908), killing 65,000 of the 80,000 Herero people as part of colonial conquest.

title: What number does the Roman numeral "D" stand for?
explanation: In Roman numerals, D represents 500; the symbol derives from the Etruscan numeral system and is used in numbers like 'MD' (1,500) and 'MDCLXVI' (1,666).

title: Which one of these was not a beach landing site in the Invasion of Normandy?
explanation: The D-Day beaches were named Gold, Juno, Sword, Omaha, and Utah; 'Silver' was not an official beach designation during the Normandy invasion.

title: What year was Canada founded in?
explanation: Canada was founded as a confederation on July 1, 1867, uniting the British colonies of Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia into the Dominion of Canada.

title: In which year was Constantinople conquered by the Turks?
explanation: Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks on May 29, 1453, when Mehmed II's forces breached the city walls after a 53-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire.

title: When did L. L. Zamenhof first publish "Unua Libro", the first publication describing his international language Esperanto?
explanation: L.L. Zamenhof published 'Unua Libro' (First Book) in 1887, introducing Esperanto, an international auxiliary language designed to promote peace among nations.

title: Where was Abraham Lincoln when he was assassinated by John Wilkes Booth in 1865?
explanation: Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C., on April 14, 1865, by actor John Wilkes Booth; Lincoln died the following morning.

title: Who assassinated President James A. Garfield?
explanation: Charles Guiteau assassinated President James A. Garfield on July 2, 1881; Garfield died on September 19, 1881, from complications of the gunshot wound.

title: Which of the following was not one of Joseph Stalin's ten blows during World War II?
explanation: The Vistula-Oder Offensive was a major Soviet operation but was NOT one of Stalin's Ten Blows; instead, it was one of the Ten Stalin Blows' successors in 1945.

title: What is the name of the Boeing B-29 that dropped the 'Little Boy' atomic bomb on Hiroshima?
explanation: The Boeing B-29 Superfortress 'Enola Gay', piloted by Colonel Paul Tibbets, dropped the 'Little Boy' atomic bomb on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945.

title: Who famously coined the phrase "I think, therefore I am"?
explanation: René Descartes formulated the philosophical statement 'Cogito, ergo sum' (I think, therefore I am) in his 1637 work 'Discourse on Method'.

title: How many manned moon landings have there been?
explanation: Six manned Apollo missions successfully landed on the Moon between 1969 and 1972 (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17), with twelve astronauts walking on the surface.

title: In World War I, what was the name of the alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire, and Bulgaria?
wrong_answers: {"The Axis Powers","The Federation of Empires","Authoritarian Alliance"}
explanation: The Central Powers alliance comprised Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire, and Bulgaria during World War I, opposing the Entente powers.

title: The ancient city of Chichén Itzá was built by which civilization?
explanation: Chichén Itzá was built by Mayan civilization around the 10th century, becoming a major Yucatan Peninsula city; it later was influenced by Toltec invaders.

title: After his loss at the Battle of Waterloo, Napoleon Bonaparte was exiled to which island?
explanation: After his defeat at the Battle of Waterloo on June 18, 1815, Napoleon Bonaparte was exiled to the remote island of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean.

title: The term Luddite originally applied to disgruntled workers in which industry?
explanation: Luddites were textile workers in early 1800s England who smashed machinery to protest low wages and job losses caused by industrial mechanization.

title: In 1939, Britain and France declared war on Germany after it invaded which country?
explanation: Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, prompted Britain and France to declare war on Germany, beginning World War II in Western Europe.

title: Which Greek god was the god of the Sun?
explanation: Helios was the ancient Greek god of the Sun, often depicted driving his solar chariot across the sky; he was later syncretized with Apollo.

title: John Moses Browning, the designer of the M1918 BAR (Browning Automatic Rifle) was a part of which religion?
explanation: John Moses Browning was a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormon); his religious faith influenced his personal values throughout his life.

title: What date was the first flight of the P-40 Warhawk?
explanation: The P-40 Warhawk had its first flight on October 14, 1938, becoming one of the most widely produced American fighters of World War II.

title: When was the "Siege of Leningrad" lifted during World War II?
explanation: The Siege of Leningrad ended on January 27, 1944, after 872 days of brutal blockade by Nazi Germany, resulting in approximately 1 million deaths from starvation.

title: What was the name of the spy ring that helped the United States win the Revolutionary War?
explanation: The Culper Ring was a spy network operated by George Washington during the Revolutionary War to gather intelligence on British movements in New York City.

title: What was the first recorded object to ever reach space?
explanation: The Bumper-WAC rocket reached space on February 24, 1949, becoming the first human-made object to reach the region defined as space (80 km altitude).

title: Who was the Prime Minister of Japan when Japan declared war on the US?
explanation: General Hideki Tojo was Japan's Prime Minister from October 1941 to July 1944, serving as the military leader who led Japan through most of World War II.

title: What war did George Orwell famously volunteer for and nearly died in?
wrong_answers: {"World War I","World War II","Russian Civil War"}
explanation: George Orwell volunteered in the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939), fighting for the Republican forces; he was shot in the throat but survived the conflict.

title: When was the city of Rome, Italy founded?
explanation: Rome was traditionally founded on April 21, 753 BCE, according to Roman legend, though archaeological evidence suggests settlement occurred earlier.

title: Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for most of World War II?
explanation: Winston Churchill served as Prime Minister from May 1940 to July 1945, leading Britain through the majority of World War II with his defiant leadership.

title: Who was the main developer of the Suez Canal?
explanation: Ferdinand de Lesseps was the French engineer who directed the construction of the Suez Canal (1859-1869), creating a crucial shortcut for global maritime trade.

title: Which Nation did NOT have a Colony in modern-day North America?
explanation: Portugal did not establish significant colonies in North America, while Spain (Florida, Southwest), Sweden (Delaware), and the Netherlands (New York) did colonize regions.

title: When did Norway become free from Sweden?
explanation: Norway declared independence from Sweden on June 7, 1905, following a union that began in 1814 after Denmark-Norway's defeat in the Napoleonic Wars.

title: What is the name of the famous Apache leader who died in 1909 at the age of 70?
explanation: Geronimo (1825-1909) was an Apache leader who fiercely resisted U.S. westward expansion; he surrendered in 1886 and died on the Fort Sill reservation.

title: All of the following are names of the Seven Warring States EXCEPT:
explanation: The Seven Warring States were Zhao, Qin, Qi, Chu, Yan, Han, and Wei; Zhai was not one of them, making it the correct answer to this 'EXCEPT' question.

title: The Second Boer War in 1899 was fought where?
explanation: The Second Boer War (1899-1902) was fought in South Africa between the British Empire and the Boer republics (Transvaal and Orange Free State).

title: Who was among those killed in the 2010 Smolensk, Russia plane crash tragedy?
explanation: Polish President Lech Kaczyński, along with 95 others, died in the Smolensk plane crash on April 10, 2010, en route to commemorate a World War II massacre.

title: Who was the Confederate general in the American Civil War?
wrong_answers: {"George A. Custer","Ulysses S. Grant","George B. McClellan"}
explanation: Robert E. Lee was the commanding general of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia, the South's most prominent military leader during the American Civil War.

title: The Battle of the Somme in World War I took place in which country?
explanation: The Battle of the Somme (July-November 1916) occurred in France, resulting in over 1 million casualties as part of World War I's trench warfare on the Western Front.

title: Who led France during the "Reign of Terror" ?
explanation: Maximilien Robespierre led the Reign of Terror (1793-1794) during the French Revolution as a member of the Committee of Public Safety before his own execution.

title: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
explanation: Augustus (Octavian) became Rome's first emperor in 27 BCE, ending the Roman Republic and establishing the Roman Empire that lasted until 476 CE.

title: In what year did the North American Video Game Crash occur?
explanation: The North American video game crash of 1983 resulted from market oversaturation, poor-quality games, and consumer loss of confidence in the home video game industry.

title: What is the name of the ship which was only a few miles away from the RMS Titanic when it struck an iceberg on April 14, 1912?
explanation: The SS Californian was nearby when the Titanic struck an iceberg on April 14, 1912, but failed to respond to distress signals, becoming emblematic of the disaster.

title: What historical event was Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture referencing?
wrong_answers: {"The American War of 1812","The Russian Revolution","The Charge of the Light Brigade (Crimean War)"}
explanation: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture commemorates the Russian defense against Napoleon's invasion in 1812, incorporating the Russian national anthem and cannon fire.

title: The pantheon in Rome was used to worship what god?
explanation: The Roman Pantheon was built to honor all gods ('any god they wanted'), as 'pantheon' literally means 'temple of all gods' in its architectural purpose.

title: What was the code name for the German invasion of the Soviet Union in WW2?
explanation: Operation Barbarossa was the Nazi code name for the June 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union, representing a massive breach of the 1939 Molotov-Ribbentrop Non-Aggression Pact.

title: What year did the Titanic sink?
explanation: The RMS Titanic sank on April 15, 1912, after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic, resulting in the deaths of approximately 1,500 passengers and crew.

title: The fraudelent doctor John R. Brinkley acummulated great fame and wealth in the early 1900s offering what service?
wrong_answers: {"Pig blood transfusion","Cow liver transplant","Turkey breast implants"}
explanation: John R. Brinkley fraudulently claimed that transplanting goat testicles into men could restore virility and vitality, accumulating a fortune from this pseudoscientific procedure.

title: What was the name of one of the surviving palaces of Henry VIII located near Richmond, London?
explanation: Hampton Court Palace was a royal residence where Henry VIII lived with his wives; built in 1514, it remains one of England's finest surviving Tudor buildings.

title: Which American civilization is the source of the belief that the world would end or drastically change on December 21st, 2012?
explanation: The Maya civilization developed the Long Count calendar, which completed a 5,125-year cycle on December 21, 2012; modern interpretations misread this astronomical event as a doomsday prediction.

title: On which day did ARPANET suffer a 4 hour long network crash?
explanation: ARPANET experienced a major routing table corruption on October 27, 1980, lasting 4 hours and affecting most of the early internet infrastructure.

title: In which years did the Battle of Gallipoli take place?
explanation: The campaign to take the Gallipoli Peninsula from Ottoman forces lasted from April 1915 through January 1916, ending in Allied withdrawal.

title: A collection of Sanskrit hymns and verses known as the Vedas are sacred texts in what religion?
explanation: The Vedas are the oldest sacred scriptures in Hinduism, composed in Sanskrit between 1500–500 BCE and forming the foundation of Hindu philosophy and ritual.

title: What year were the Marian Reforms instituted in the Roman Republic?
explanation: Gaius Marius implemented military reforms in 107 BCE that professionalized the Roman army, introducing recruitment of landless citizens and changing legion structure.

title: How old was Lyndon B. Johnson when he assumed the role of President of the United States?
explanation: Lyndon B. Johnson was born August 27, 1908 and assumed the presidency on November 22, 1963, making him 55 years old.

title: What age was King Henry V when he died?
explanation: Henry V was born in 1387 and died on August 31, 1422 at age 34 (turning 35 later that year), succumbing to dysentery during the Hundred Years' War.

title: Which of the following is not in the Indo-European language family?
explanation: Finnish belongs to the Uralic language family, not Indo-European; English, Hindi, and Russian all descend from the ancient Indo-European language stock.

title: In which country was the Statue of Liberty built and exported to the United States of America?
explanation: French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi designed the Statue of Liberty and it was constructed in France before being disassembled and shipped to New York in 1885.

title: Joseph Smith was the founder of what religion?
explanation: Joseph Smith founded the Latter-day Saint movement in 1830, claiming to have received divine revelation and translated the Book of Mormon.

title: What Southeast Asian country was formerly known as 'Lan Xang'?
explanation: Lan Xang, meaning 'Land of a Million Elephants,' was the ancient kingdom that occupied present-day Laos from the 14th to 18th centuries.

title: Before the American colonies switched to the Gregorian calendar in 1752, on what date did their new year start?
explanation: Before adopting the Gregorian calendar, British colonies used the Julian calendar where the new year began on March 25th (Lady Day), not January 1st.

title: How long did the Warsaw Uprising during World War II last?
explanation: The Warsaw Uprising lasted from August 1 to October 2, 1944, representing 63 days of Polish resistance against Nazi occupation before its brutal suppression.

title: Which of the following Physicists aided Nazi Germany in their production of a nuclear weapon?
explanation: Werner Heisenberg led Germany's nuclear research program during WWII and worked to develop atomic weapons, though the project ultimately failed to produce a bomb.

title: What year was the first Pizza Hut restaurant opened?
explanation: Pizza Hut was founded by Frank and Dan Carney in Wichita, Kansas on May 18, 1958, becoming the first sit-down pizza chain.

title: What was the aim of the "Umbrella Revolution" in Hong Kong in 2014?
wrong_answers: {"Gaining Independence","Go back under British Rule","Lower taxes"}
explanation: The 2014 Umbrella Revolution in Hong Kong was primarily a movement demanding direct universal suffrage for electing the Chief Executive.

title: When did the United States formally declare war on Japan, entering World War II?
explanation: The U.S. declared war on Japan on December 8, 1941 (the day after Pearl Harbor), formally bringing America into World War II.

title: Who was the first Chancellor of a united Germany in 1871?
explanation: Otto von Bismarck was the Iron Chancellor who unified Germany through diplomatic maneuvering and the Franco-Prussian War, becoming chancellor in 1871.

title: Which Roman Emperor led the Roman Empire to reach its maximum territorial extent?
explanation: Emperor Trajan (98–117 AD) expanded the Roman Empire to its largest territorial extent, conquering Dacia, Mesopotamia, and the Caucasus region.

title: Who was the last Roman emperor in the Year of Four Emperors (69 AD)?
explanation: Vespasian emerged victorious from the Year of Four Emperors (69 AD) after defeats of Galba, Otho, and Vitellius, establishing the Flavian dynasty.

title: When was the Grand Patriotic War in the USSR concluded?
explanation: May 9, 1945 marks Victory in Europe Day for the Soviet Union, when Nazi Germany formally surrendered, ending the Great Patriotic War in the USSR.

title: Who was the President of the United States during the signing of the Gadsden Purchase?
explanation: Franklin Pierce was president when the Gadsden Purchase was signed in December 1853, acquiring land in present-day southern Arizona and New Mexico.

title: Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand?
explanation: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist, assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand on June 28, 1914, triggering the chain of events leading to World War I.

title: In what year did the Wall Street Crash take place?
explanation: The Wall Street Crash occurred on October 29, 1929 ('Black Tuesday'), marking the start of the Great Depression in the United States.

title: In what prison was Adolf Hitler held in 1924?
