explanation: Adolf Hitler served his prison sentence for the failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch at Landsberg Prison in Bavaria, where he wrote 'Mein Kampf'.

title: What was the total length of the Titanic?
explanation: The RMS Titanic was 882 feet (268.8 meters) long, making it one of the largest ships of its era when it sank in 1912.

title: When did the Crisis of the Third Century begin?
explanation: The Crisis of the Third Century began in 235 AD when Emperor Severus Alexander was assassinated, starting a period of military anarchy and civil war.

title: In which one of these cities did the Great Stink of 1858 occur?
explanation: The Great Stink of 1858 occurred in London when the Thames River became severely polluted, creating such noxious odors that Parliament temporarily relocated.

title: What was the name of the chemical that was dropped on Vietnam during the Vietnam war?
explanation: Agent Orange was a herbicide used by the U.S. military during the Vietnam War to defoliate jungle areas and destroy crops.

title: How did the Vikings call their short-lived colony in today's Canada?
explanation: The Vikings called their North American settlement Vínland, named after wild grapes they found there; it is believed to be present-day Newfoundland.

title: The creator of the Enigma Cypher and Machine was of what nationality?
explanation: Arthur Scherbius, a German inventor, created the Enigma cipher machine in the 1920s; it was later improved and adopted by the Nazi military.

title: When did the Battle of the Bulge end?
explanation: The Battle of the Bulge, Germany's last major offensive, lasted from December 16, 1944 to January 25, 1945 in the Ardennes region.

title: When did Norway get its constitution?
explanation: Norway adopted its constitution on May 17, 1814, establishing it as an independent constitutional monarchy after the Napoleonic Wars.

title: How many teeth does an adult rabbit have?
explanation: Adult rabbits have 28 teeth total: 6 upper and 6 lower incisors, plus molars and premolars, designed for grinding tough vegetation.

title: What is the average amount of chinchillas born into a single litter?
explanation: Chinchillas typically give birth to 1–6 kits per litter, with an average of 2–3 offspring after a gestation period of about 111 days.

title: Which of the following is NOT a venomous snake?
explanation: The reticulated python is a non-venomous constrictor, while the other three are all highly venomous snakes found in Asia and Australia.

title: For what reason would a spotted hyena "laugh"?
explanation: Spotted hyenas produce their distinctive 'laugh' as a vocalization expressing nervousness or anxiety, not amusement or aggression.

title: What color is a Steller's Jay?
wrong_answers: {"blue and grey","blue and white","grey and black"}
explanation: The Steller's Jay is a bright blue and black bird found in western North America, easily recognized by its blue and black plumage.

title: What is the average lifespan of a domestic rabbit?
explanation: Domestic rabbits live an average of 8–12 years with proper care, though some have been known to reach their late teens.

title: What is the collective noun for a group of crows?
explanation: A group of crows is called a murder, derived from medieval folklore that associated the dark birds with death and omens.

title: What is the fastest animal?
explanation: The peregrine falcon reaches speeds over 240 mph during its hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth by a significant margin.

title: Chronic Wasting Disease (CWD) exclusively infects members of which family of animals?
explanation: Chronic Wasting Disease exclusively infects members of the Cervidae family, including deer, elk, and moose.

title: A carnivorous animal eats flesh, what does a nucivorous animal eat?
explanation: A nucivorous animal is one that feeds on nuts; the term comes from the Latin 'nux' meaning nut.

title: What color/colour is a polar bear's skin?
explanation: Polar bear skin is black, which absorbs heat from the sun; their white fur reflects light and provides camouflage in Arctic ice.

title: Which of these animals are not real?
explanation: The Nemean Lion was a mythological creature from Greek legend, while the sea dragon, Tasmanian devil, and giant squid are all real animal species.

title: What is the scientific name of the Common Chimpanzee?
explanation: Pan troglodytes is the scientific binomial name for the common chimpanzee, classified in the genus Pan.

title: What was the name of the Ethiopian Wolf before they knew it was related to wolves?
explanation: Before genetic studies confirmed its wolf ancestry, the Ethiopian wolf was called the Simien Jackal due to its jackal-like appearance.

title: "Decapods" are an order of ten-footed crustaceans. Which of these are NOT decapods?
explanation: Krill are small shrimp-like crustaceans with only six legs, placing them in the order Euphausiacea, not the ten-legged decapods.

title: What is the collective noun for vultures?
explanation: A group of vultures is called a wake, particularly when they're gathered at a carcass feeding together.

title: What is the scientific name of the cheetah?
explanation: Acinonyx jubatus is the scientific name for the cheetah, distinguished by its slender build, non-retractable claws, and semi-retractable claws adapted for speed.

title: Which animal was part of an Russian domestication experiment in 1959?
explanation: Russian scientist Dmitry Belyaev began a domestication experiment with foxes in 1959, demonstrating rapid behavioral and physical changes through selective breeding.

title: Which of these species is not extinct?
explanation: The Komodo dragon remains extant in the Lesser Sunda Islands of Indonesia, while the other three species are all extinct.

title: Which breed of dog is traditionally associated with firefighters?
explanation: Dalmatians were historically used as firehouse dogs to run alongside horse-drawn fire engines, and the tradition continues symbolically today.

title: The dish Fugu, is made from what family of fish?
explanation: Fugu is prepared from pufferfish, which contain tetrodotoxin in their organs; the dish requires specially licensed chefs trained to remove toxic parts.

title: To which biological phylum do all mammals, birds and reptiles belong?
explanation: Chordata is the phylum containing all vertebrates with notochords (or backbones), including mammals, birds, and reptiles.

title: What dog breed is one of the oldest breeds of dog and has flourished since before 400 BCE.
explanation: Pugs have been documented as a breed since before 400 BCE in China, making them one of the oldest dog breeds with continuous recorded history.

title: What is the fastest land animal?
explanation: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching speeds of 70 mph during pursuits, relying on acceleration rather than sustained running.

title: Which species of Brown Bear is not extinct?
explanation: The Syrian brown bear (Ursus arctos syriacus) still inhabits small regions of the Middle East, while the other subspecies are extinct.

title: Which class of animals are newts members of?
explanation: Newts belong to the class Amphibia, sharing characteristics with frogs and salamanders including moist skin and aquatic larval stages.

title: What are rhino's horn made of?
explanation: Rhino horns are made of keratin, the same protein found in human hair and nails, not bone or ivory as commonly believed.

title: About how much of their body weight in food do sea otters eat every day?
explanation: Sea otters consume approximately 25% of their body weight daily in food to maintain their high metabolism and insulate their fur.

title: What is the scientific name for the "Polar Bear"?
explanation: Ursus maritimus is the scientific name for the polar bear, derived from Latin meaning 'sea bear' due to its marine Arctic habitat.

title: Which species is a "mountain chicken"?
explanation: The mountain chicken is a large frog species native to the West Indies, named for its meat which allegedly tastes like chicken.

title: By definition, where does an abyssopelagic animal live?
correct_answer: At the bottom of the ocean
wrong_answers: {"In the desert","On top of a mountain","Inside a tree"}
explanation: By definition, abyssopelagic animals live in the deepest regions of the ocean at depths below 6,000 meters near the seafloor.

title: What is the Gray Wolf's scientific name?
explanation: Canis lupus is the scientific name for the gray wolf, with lupus being the Latin word for wolf.

title: The now extinct species "Thylacine" was native to where?
explanation: The thylacine (Tasmanian tiger) was native exclusively to Tasmania, Australia, and was hunted to extinction by the early 20th century.

title: Which of the following is true when alligators are behaving territorially?
correct_answer: They bellow while showing their tail and neck
wrong_answers: {"Open their jaws while making a clicking noise","They run full force at the threat","Slap their tails on the ground"}
explanation: Territorial alligators produce loud bellows while simultaneously raising and swaying their head, tail, and neck as visual and acoustic displays.

title: The Kākāpō is a large, flightless, nocturnal parrot native to which country?
explanation: The Kākāpō is a critically endangered, flightless, nocturnal parrot endemic to New Zealand, one of the world's rarest birds.

title: Which of the following is another name for the "Poecilotheria Metallica Tarantula"?
explanation: The Poecilotheria Metallica is commonly called the Gooty sapphire ornamental tarantula, named after Gooty, a village in India.

title: What is the collective noun for bears?
explanation: A collective noun for bears is a sloth, referencing their characteristically slow, deliberate movements through the forest.

title: Which dog breed is named after a region in Croatia
explanation: The Dalmatian dog breed is named after Dalmatia, a historical region on the Adriatic coast of Croatia.

title: What is the name for a male bee that comes from an unfertilized egg?
explanation: A drone is a male honeybee that develops from an unfertilized egg; drones exist solely to mate with virgin queens.

title: What is the collective noun for rats?
explanation: A group of rats is called a mischief, evoking the chaos and destruction that rats cause when gathered in large numbers.

title: What does "hippopotamus" mean and in what langauge?
explanation: Hippopotamus comes from Greek, combining 'hippos' (river) and 'potamos' (horse), literally meaning 'river horse'.

title: What bird is born with claws on its wing digits?
explanation: The hoatzin chick is born with two claws on its wing digits that allow it to climb branches, a primitive trait among modern birds.

title: What is the scientific name of the Budgerigar?
explanation: Melopsittacus undulatus is the scientific name for the budgerigar or parakeet, commonly kept as pets in households worldwide.

title: Which of these is a colony of polyps and not a jellyfish?
explanation: The Portuguese Man-of-War is a colonial organism composed of specialized polyps working together, not a single jellyfish entity.

title: How many legs do butterflies have?
explanation: Butterflies have six legs (three pairs), like all insects in the class Insecta, arranged in segments along their thorax.

title: What is the name of a rabbit's abode?
explanation: A rabbit's abode is called a burrow, an underground tunnel system where wild rabbits live, breed, and take shelter.

title: Hippocampus is the Latin name for which marine creature?
explanation: Hippocampus is the Latin/Greek scientific name for the seahorse, a small marine fish with a horse-like head and prehensile tail.

title: What is the name of the copper-rich protein that creates the blue blood in the Antarctic octopus?
explanation: Hemocyanin is a copper-containing protein that functions as an oxygen carrier in the blood of cephalopods and arthropods, producing blue blood.

title: What is the national bird of Bahrain?
explanation: The bulbul is the national bird of Bahrain, a small passerine bird widespread throughout the Middle East and Asia.

title: What is the scientific name for modern day humans?
explanation: Homo sapiens is the scientific binomial name for modern humans, meaning 'wise man' in Latin.

title: What is the past tense of "go"?
explanation: The past tense of 'go' is 'went', an irregular verb that does not follow the standard -ed ending pattern of regular English verbs.

title: What is the plural of "child"?
explanation: The plural of 'child' is 'children', an irregular plural form inherited from Old English and one of the most common exceptions to regular pluralization.

title: Which article goes before "university"?
explanation: The article 'a' is used before 'university' because the word begins with a consonant sound /j/, even though it starts with a vowel letter.

title: Which word means "happy"?
explanation: Joyful is a synonym for 'happy', expressing a state of great pleasure or contentment.

title: What is the past tense of "see"?
explanation: The past tense of 'see' is 'saw', an irregular strong verb whose stem changes from see to saw.

title: What is the plural of "mouse" (the animal)?
explanation: The plural of 'mouse' (the animal) is 'mice', an irregular plural inherited from Germanic languages rather than the regular -s ending.

title: Which article goes before "hour"?
explanation: The article 'an' is used before 'hour' because the word is pronounced with a silent 'h' /aʊr/, making it begin with a vowel sound.

title: Complete the idiom: "It's raining cats and ___".
explanation: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is an idiomatic expression meaning heavy rain, likely derived from mythology or 17th-century images of felines and canines.

title: What is the past tense of "eat"?
explanation: The past tense of 'eat' is 'ate', a strong irregular verb where the vowel changes from 'ea' to a shorter 'a' sound.

title: Which word is a synonym of "begin"?
explanation: 'Start' is a synonym for 'begin', meaning to initiate or set something in motion.

title: What is the plural of "foot"?
explanation: The plural of 'foot' is 'feet', an irregular plural form derived from Old English where singular and plural vowels differ.

title: What is the past tense of "buy"?
explanation: The past tense of 'buy' is 'bought', an irregular verb with both stem and pronunciation changes not following the regular -ed pattern.

title: What is the past tense of "swim"?
explanation: The past tense of 'swim' is 'swam', a strong irregular verb where the middle vowel changes, while 'swum' is actually the past participle.

title: Complete the idiom: "It's a piece of ___" (meaning easy).
explanation: 'It's a piece of cake' is an idiom meaning something is easy to do, possibly referencing how cake is simple and pleasant to eat.

title: What does "procrastinate" mean?
wrong_answers: {"to act quickly","to plan ahead","to finish a task"}
explanation: 'Procrastinate' means to delay or postpone something, often unnecessarily or until the last moment.

title: What is the comparative form of "good"?
explanation: The comparative form of 'good' is 'better', an irregular comparison that changes the base word entirely rather than adding -er.

title: What is the antonym of "ancient"?
explanation: 'Modern' is the antonym of 'ancient', referring to things that are current or recent rather than from the distant past.

title: What does the idiom "break a leg" mean?
explanation: The idiom originated in theater to wish performers good luck, possibly because saying the opposite was considered superstition.

title: What is the past tense of "think"?
explanation: In English, most irregular verbs follow strong vowel change patterns; "think" becomes "thought" rather than following the regular -ed ending.

title: Which word means "to make something clear by giving examples"?
explanation: The word "illustrate" comes from Latin and specifically means to clarify or explain a concept through concrete examples.

title: What is the past participle of "write"?
explanation: "Written" is the standard past participle of "write" in English; it derives from the Old English strong verb class.

title: Which word is a synonym of "reluctant"?
explanation: "Unwilling" is the direct synonym for reluctant, both describing the state of being resistant or averse to something.

title: What does "ephemeral" mean?
explanation: Ephemeral derives from Greek "ephemeros" (lasting one day) and describes things that are short-lived or transitory.

title: What does "ubiquitous" mean?
explanation: "Ubiquitous" comes from Latin "ubique" meaning "everywhere," describing something that is found or present in all places.

title: Which is the plural of "octopus" most accepted by modern dictionaries?
explanation: Modern English dictionaries accept "octopuses" as the standard plural; while "octopi" and "octopodes" exist, the -es form is most widely recognized.

title: What does "pleonasm" describe?
wrong_answers: {"a verse meter","a dance step","a type of bird"}
explanation: Pleonasm is derived from Greek "pleonasmós" and refers to the use of redundant or excessive words for emphasis.

title: What does "disinterested" properly mean?
explanation: "Disinterested" originally meant impartial or unbiased (without self-interest), distinct from "uninterested" which means lacking interest.

title: What does "penultimate" mean?
wrong_answers: {"the very last","the very first","the very best"}
explanation: "Penultimate" comes from Latin "paenultimus" meaning "almost last," referring to the second-to-last position in a sequence.

title: In the second conditional, complete: "If I ___ rich, I would travel the world."
explanation: The second conditional requires "were" even with first-person singular subjects to express counterfactual situations in formal English.

title: What does "esoteric" mean?
correct_answer: understood by only a small group
explanation: "Esoteric" derives from Greek and describes knowledge or teachings intended for only a select, initiated group.

title: What does "cacophony" describe?
correct_answer: a harsh, jarring mixture of sounds
explanation: "Cacophony" comes from Greek "kakophonia" (bad sound) and describes a discordant or harshly chaotic mixture of sounds.

title: How many bones does an adult human have?
explanation: An adult human skeleton contains 206 bones; infants are born with more, but many fuse together as they mature.

title: Which organ produces insulin?
explanation: The pancreas contains beta cells in the islets of Langerhans that secrete insulin to regulate blood glucose levels.

title: What is the largest organ of the human body?
explanation: The skin is the largest organ, covering the entire body surface and typically weighing 8-10 pounds in adults.

title: How many chambers does the human heart have?
explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles that pump blood through pulmonary and systemic circulation.

title: How many teeth does a typical adult human have?
explanation: Adults typically have 32 teeth: 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, and 12 molars (including wisdom teeth).

title: What is the normal human body temperature in Celsius?
explanation: Normal human body temperature averages 37°C (98.6°F); this is the baseline for fever detection in clinical settings.

title: Which blood cells primarily fight infection?
explanation: White blood cells (leukocytes) are the immune system's primary defense, fighting bacterial, viral, and other pathogens.

title: What does "BMI" stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Bone Mass Indicator","Blood Movement Index","Basic Metabolic Indicator"}
explanation: BMI (Body Mass Index) is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared, used to screen weight categories.

title: Which vitamin does the skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
explanation: Skin cells synthesize cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) when exposed to UV-B radiation, essential for calcium absorption and bone health.

title: Which organ filters blood and produces urine?
explanation: The kidneys filter metabolic waste and excess water from the blood to form urine, maintaining electrolyte and fluid balance.

title: What does "CPR" stand for?
wrong_answers: {"Critical patient response","Coronary pulse recovery","Cardiac pressure relief"}
explanation: CPR (Cardiopulmonary resuscitation) combines chest compressions and rescue breathing to maintain circulation during cardiac arrest.

title: What are the four main blood groups in the ABO system?
explanation: The ABO system has four blood groups: A, B, AB, and O, determined by the presence of antigens on red blood cells.

title: What is the normal resting heart rate range for an adult?
explanation: A healthy adult resting heart rate typically ranges from 60-100 beats per minute; athletes often have lower rates.

title: What is the medical term for high blood pressure?
explanation: Hypertension is the medical term for persistently elevated blood pressure, defined as ≥130/80 mmHg in current guidelines.

title: How many chromosomes does a typical human cell have?
explanation: Human cells contain 46 chromosomes: 23 pairs inherited from each parent, with 22 autosomes and 1 sex chromosome pair.

title: Vitamin C deficiency causes which disease?
explanation: Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency, preventing collagen synthesis and leading to bleeding, weak wounds, and historical prevalence among sailors.

title: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters?
explanation: The iris is a muscular diaphragm that controls pupil size, regulating how much light reaches the retina for optimal vision.

title: Which gland is often called the body's "master gland"?
explanation: The pituitary gland produces hormones that regulate growth, reproduction, and metabolism, controlling other endocrine glands throughout the body.

title: What is the largest artery in the human body?
explanation: The aorta is the main artery exiting the left ventricle, delivering oxygenated blood to the entire body at high pressure.

title: Which nutrient provides 9 kcal per gram?
explanation: Fat provides 9 kilocalories per gram, while both protein and carbohydrates provide 4 kcal/g, making fat the most energy-dense macronutrient.

title: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
explanation: The stapes (stirrup bone) in the middle ear is the smallest human bone, measuring about 3.5 mm, crucial for sound transmission.

title: Which cells in the pancreas produce insulin?
explanation: Beta cells located in pancreatic islets of Langerhans secrete insulin in response to elevated blood glucose levels.

title: What does "DNA" stand for?
explanation: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is the molecule storing genetic instructions; "deoxyribo" refers to the sugar lacking one oxygen atom.

title: Which neurotransmitter is most associated with reward and motivation?
explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter most associated with reward, motivation, and pleasure in the brain's limbic and prefrontal systems.

title: Which doctor is regarded as the father of modern medicine?
explanation: Hippocrates (c. 460-370 BCE) is called the father of modern medicine for establishing ethical medical practice and the Hippocratic Oath.
